title: Weekend Warm-up: Germany’s roster tiers broken down for the future and MORE!
description: Germany is entering a new era.
fullText:
The German national team has established its future with Jürgen Klopp and the former Liverpool boss will get going on figuring our what went wrong in the past, where things stand in the present, and how to get Germany where it needs to be for the future.

One of the first tasks for Klopp and Co. will be to assess the roster that was called up for the World Cup. To get out in front of that exercise, BFW has compiled a tiered ranking for the squad — plus some (not all) other candidates for the future. Let’s begin…

Manuel Neuer (40), Goalkeeper: Germany just needs to turn the page and move on. As it stands, Neuer likely will not be around much longer anyway as it is assumed that he will retire.

Antonio Rüdiger (33), Defense: This is a natural breaking off point for the Real Madrid veteran, who actually played well at the World Cup. The transition to new players on the backline must begin and the temptation to lean on Rüdiger should be avoided.

Leon Goretzka, Midfield (31): Goretzka’s time has come. He actually had a moment or two in the World Cup, but it is time to turn the page.

Pascal Groß, Midfield (35): Truthfully, there is no good reason that Groß was called in for this World Cup.

Leroy Sané, Attack (30): Do we really need to lay out why?

Oliver Baumann (36), Goalkeeper: Unfortunately, Baumann might have missed his window and it is probably time to just move on. After a bad second half with Hoffenheim, Baumann has nothing left to show and what he has just is not going to be good enough for the future. Still, he could be a veteran presence to help guide younger goalkeepers.

Waldemar Anton, Defense (30): Anton will be 34-years-old by the next World Cup. The tough decision will be — do you keep him around as a stable, veteran defender or just cut ties now?

David Raum, Defense (28): The RB Leipzig star is still just 28-years-old, but injury and an emerging Nathaniel Brown cost him his starting job. Can he stay healthy enough to be a factor in 2030? This will likely come down to Klopp’s preference for what he wants out of the position.

Nadiem Amiri (29), Midfield: Some will say that Amiri played well and that he deserves another chance. That would be a valid argument, but it will up to Klopp on how he see the vertan Mainz 05 midfielder.

Maximilian Beier (23), Attack: Beier seems like a player who will perpetually be on the fringe of the roster. At that point, is it even worth calling him up? During a tournament where offense was hard to come by, Beier was barely used. Maybe Klopp can revisit using Beier later, but unless the new boss sees something that Nagelsmann did not (entirely possible by the way), Germany might want to give some others a chance.

Deniz Undav (30): Undav is right on the cusp of being left out because of his age. The biggest factor for him is how things go physically for the next four years. It is easy to imagine him being the veteran attacker along for the ride, but Klopp might wan to go in a different direction.

Malick Thiaw (24): At 24-years-old, Thiaw is nearing the time where he will have to show that he can be a serious contender for a starting role. His inclusion into the World Cup felt more like a “who else do we have?” deal than Nagelsmann identifying a player, who could legitimately help. Opportunity could knock for Thiaw under Klopp, but he will have to take full advantage of it.

Assan Ouédraogo (20): It is still perplexing to understand what Nagelsmann’s intent was to call Ouédraogo up after Lennart Karl’s injury. The RB Leipzig youngster had no chance for playing time and could offer no help to positions like wing or right-back where Germany needed help. That said, he is a name to know for the future. His development in the coming years is one that Klopp will need to be aware. Still so young, Ouédraogo could truly grow into a longtime role…or just fade into being the answer to a trivia question years from now.

Alexander Nübel (29): There is a possibility that Nübel is just “good”, but that might be enough to stick around for one of the three goalkeeper spots.

Jonathan Tah (30): Similar to Anton, Tah will be 34-years-old at the next World Cup, but he is currently a starter and is considered a leader on the squad. He could play throughout this cycle and eventually ease into the same role that Rüdiger had this year.

Aleksandar Pavlović (22): Pavlović really hurt his reputation at the World Cup. At a time where he should cemented his role for the next decade, the Bayern Munich midfielder under-performed and open the door for another midfielder to slide in. If Kimmich is retained and shifts to the midfield, Pavlović could be in a tough spot for the starting XI.

Felix Nmecha (25): Similar to Pavlović, but older, Nmecha was the darling of fans for 1.5 games. Then, reality struck and Nmecha became a liability in the last 2.5 games. As of now, he should not be guaranteed anything except another look.

Jamie Leweling (25): Leweling is in a similar boat to Beier, but not quite the same. Both players are versatile and Beier is the faster player, but there seems to be more trust in Leweling (despite his lack of action at the World Cup). Leweling’s performances for VfB Stuttgart will likely play a massive role in how he fits in moving forward.

Angelo Stiller (25): It is fair to ask how shaky Stiller was if he could not convince Nagelsmann to make a change in the midfield. That said, Nagelsmann’s notoriously stubborn decision-making could actually lend to Stiller getting a closer look from Klopp.

Kai Havertz (27): Havertz continues to be the darling of every Germany coach, which is puzzling. A good player, but not a game-changer, Havertz continues to eat up minutes at a position where he is not a prime producer. How much longer can this go on? The Arsenal man seems to have great timing in that that whenever he starts to be put under the gun. he manages a strong performance. The downside is that there are just not enough of them to warrant being a consistent starting striker.

Nick Woltemade (24): A year ago, Woltemade seemed like he might be be Germany’s striker for the next decade. After spending a harrowing year with Newcastle United, though, Woltemade does not have a position, lacks confidence, and might not make the next call-up list. His situation with NUFC could be a ticking time bomb.

Jamal Musiala (23): The most complicated name in this tier. In theory, Musiala should be a no-brainer, but his performance for Bayern Munich and Germany has left a lot to be desired and a lot of doubt. Also, there is the specter of him being demanding about playing time and what position he plays. A true general like Klopp can sort out if those things are truly an issue. If so, Musiala might have a rude awakening. The other side of this is Musiala’s health. He is still not 100% after his catastrophic leg injury, but this could be as good as it gets. What could help Musiala immensely, is if he opens himself up to playing wing full-time for the German national team, where the squad desperately needs him. As an attacking midfielder — right now — Musiala lacks the physicality, vision, and willingness to be a facilitator to help Germany operate at its best.

Joshua Kimmich (31): Kimmich needs to return to the midfield and take part in the transition to the next generation. As captain, he is still a valuable player and assuming he is still playing at an acceptable level in 2030, he could be a nice veteran to have on the bench.

Lennart Karl (18): Karl is the future of Germany’s attack.

Florian Wirtz (23): So, what is the difference between Wirtz and Musiala? Musiala has the specter of what his ceiling is after his brutal leg/ankle injury. Right now, even not at his best, Wirtz is the stronger player. Musiala also gets docked points for his position (attacking midfield) where he has struggled mightily, yet continued to play there until it was too late under Nagelsmann. It is fair to ask why? Coaching incompetence and the inability to see what was obvious all season…or pressure from the player? A clear answer to that could help Musiala’s case.

Nathaniel Brown (23): The breakout star for Germany, his slot at left-back should be filled for the next two World Cup cycles.

Nico Schlotterbeck (26): Injured for the majority of this World Cup, Schlotterbeck was sorely missed. The Borussia Dortmund defender should be the formal leader on the backline moving forward.

Jonas Urbig (22): If Urbig continues on his current trajectory, he should be the starter in between the sticks in for 2030.

Tom Bischof (21): People will say that Bischof should not have been called up for this World Cup because of the way he was used (or not used) at Bayern Munich last season. However, everything Bischof brings to the table — physicality, a scoring threat, versatility — were things missing from Germany’s midfield and roster overall. Moreover, if he stayed at Hoffenheim, he would have been a shoo-in for a roster spot. Now, there will be a strong focus on how he plays for Bayern Munich this season. If he excels, it is not hard to imagine him competing for a starting role at some point during this cycle.

Brajan Gruda (21): A player on the periphery while at Mainz, his move to Brighton & Hove Albion put him “out of sight, out of mind.” Now, Gruda is back with RB Leipzig again on loan and could thrust himself back into the mix with a good showing this season.

Marc-André ter Stegen (34): If healthy, Ter Stegen could be a top three goalkeeper for Germany, but his health and viability are both major question marks at this point. Ter Stegen could get a new lease on life with Ajax (if the move goes through), but he still feels like a longshot. When factoring in his unhappiness with sitting behind Neuer all of those years, Klopp might just opt to move on completely.

Yan Aurel Bisseck (25): At his age, Bisseck is what he is. There will not be a marked change in how he performs. That should be enough to at least warrant a look from Klopp.

Anton Stach (27): Stach should have been called up over Groß, but the ball is firmly in Stach’s court. Perform and Klopp will — at least — look over to check him out. There is no room for error for Stach, though.

Chris Fuhrich (28): The VfB Stuttgart man is just a solid, professional winger. While he does nothing spectacular, his presence and understanding of how to properly play the position could be valuable in a bench role. As of now, though, it feels like he missed his window.

Nicolo Tresoldi (21): The youngster is seeing his star quickly rise and could end up being Germany’s best option for the No. 9 position in 2030. Does Klopp see it that way?

Kevin Schade (24): Schade is solid, but is he anything more? Klopp should seek to find out and quickly.

Said El Mala (19): El Mala is undoubtedly a talent, but his maturity might be what kept him off the squad this summer. Will Klopp look to mold the youngster’s ability into something productive for Germany? It feels like it.

Karim Adeyemi (24): Adeyemi’s chances likely hinge on Hansi Flick’s ability to unlock the best of him at FC Barcelona. Germany needs wingers and Adeyemi is still young.

Maximilian Mittelstädt (29): Mittelstädt was a bizarre omission from the team this summer and could be aged out for 2023 given the position he plays (left-back), but Klopp might need some stability and consistency on the roster — at least at the beginning of the cycle.

Sometimes we delve into the archives and other times we admire (relatively) modern rock. For this edition, we are only going back to the last decade to appreciate an underrated band — Cage the Elephant.

While we have featured other songs from Cage the Elephant here, “Shake Me Down” was one of those first songs that caught my attention. Released in late 2010 on the “Thank You, Happy Birthday” album, this one has stuck with for 16 (!) years. Enjoy:

I know…I know. I have lowered my expectations, but I have enjoyed the season (even with its flaws) so far. Let’s dive in:

Ormund Hightower continues to steal the show and his ward, Daeron Targaryen seems like he is starting to embrace a bigger role in the overall storyline.

If not for Daemon, Ormund Hightower might be the show’s best character. Daemon is still the scene stealer of the show and is carrying it at times.

It is tough to pinpoint the problem with Rhaenyra, but she struggles to really capture the scenes that she is in. Eerily, this is similar to Viserys (her father) when he was on screen. There does not appear to be an issue with the way that either actor portrayed their respective characters, but it could come down to dialogue.

It was good to see Aemond back in action, but storyline is just waltzing along too slowly.

It feels like the slaughter of the City Watch will be a plotpoint that does not fully live up to the amount of time it is occupying. Hopefully, it does. One thing it has going for it is that Daemon is heavily involved.

The Ser Criston Cole storyline has been a little disappointing for such a great character. It would have been awesome to see him in more actual battles or at least in a few skirmishes. So far, his story has been one of sulking, lamentation, and the acceptance that he will die.

It is tough to discern the point of Mysaria right now.

The secret doorway at the end of the episode was…weird. It is hard to figure out what the writers are going for with that.

Overall, it was a solid episode. Admittedly, I’m moving the goalposts here because this season — while flawed (and believe me, this could turn into major issue in the homestretch of the season) — is markedly better than the first two season. At a time, where I need to shut my brain down a bit at the very end of the week, House of the Dragon — at a minimum — gives me that.

It is tough to know how Bayern Munich’s friendly vs. SV Wehen Wiesbaden will play out give how many of Bayern Munich’s regular players will be missing. A slew of youth players will likely be in the spotlight, but Tom Bischof, João Palhinha, Sacha Boey, Arijon Ibrahimović, and Sven Ulreich are expected to lead the way. From there, it will be Romper Room — and that should be kind of fun.

Prediction: SV Wehen Wiesbaden 0-4 Bayern Munich

title: Viral Video Of Dylan Larkin Has Red Wings Fans Talking
description: A new offseason video shows Dylan Larkin training in Red Wings gear, fueling speculation about his future in Detroit.
fullText:
A new offseason video featuring Dylan Larkin has Red Wings fans wondering if the trade saga may not be over after all.

Just days after Steve Yzerman stepped down as Detroit Red Wings general manager, a new video circulating on social media has sparked fresh speculation about captain Dylan Larkin’s future.

The clip, originally shared to Larkin’s Instagram Story and reposted by Crunch Time Sports, shows the Red Wings captain going through an offseason skating workout while wearing Detroit Red Wings gear.

For a fan base that has spent the summer following trade rumors, it didn’t take long for the video to generate conversation.

At first glance, seeing Larkin train in Red Wings apparel may seem noteworthy.

After all, reports throughout the offseason have indicated that the 30-year-old requested a trade following Detroit’s disappointing 2025-26 season. More recently, Steve Yzerman stepped aside as general manager, removing the executive many believed was at the center of the reported rift.

Could this video be a hint that the relationship has been repaired?

But it’s important not to read too much into it.

Many NHL players routinely train in team-issued gear during the offseason, regardless of contract situations or trade speculation. Wearing Red Wings apparel alone is not evidence that Larkin has withdrawn his trade request or that a reconciliation has already taken place.

What makes the video interesting is its timing.

It surfaced shortly after Detroit’s front office underwent its biggest change in years, leaving many to wonder whether new leadership could open the door for renewed conversations between Larkin and the organization.

Earlier reports suggested Larkin’s frustrations were tied to the previous hockey operations leadership. With that situation now changing, there is at least a path for both sides to revisit their relationship before training camp.

As encouraging as the video may be for optimistic Red Wings fans, there has been no public indication that Larkin has rescinded his reported trade request or that the two sides have formally reconciled.

For now, it’s simply an offseason training clip that has captured the attention of Hockeytown.

Whether it ultimately becomes the first sign of a fresh start or merely another moment fans analyze during a dramatic offseason remains to be seen.

title: Cubs roster move: James Triantos called up, Kevin Alcántara optioned
description: The second-round pick of the Cubs in 2021 will make his MLB debut.
fullText:
This is a really interesting roster move.

James Triantos was the Cubs’ second-round pick in 2021 out of high school in Virginia. He had just turned 18, and went right to work in the Arizona Complex League, batting .327/.376/.594 in 25 games.

He rose through the system, hitting pretty well at every stop, but never really having a position. He played all three outfield positions as well as second base and third base. This year at Triple-A Iowa, Triantos is batting .306/.344/.440 (107-for-350) with 24 doubles, seven home runs and 18 stolen bases in 85 games.

The Cubs have called up Triantos, who is now 23, to join the 26-man active roster as the team opens a series in Pittsburgh. To make room on the 26-man active roster, outfielder/DH Kevin Alcántara was optioned to Iowa. This move has not yet been officially announced by the team, but Triantos posted on his Instagram story that he was being called up, and the Cubs transactions page shows that Alcántara was optioned on Thursday.

This move appears to acknowledge that Matt Shaw isn’t close to coming back, as Triantos plays basically the same positions Shaw does. This year Triantos has played mostly second base and third base and less outfield, while last year he played a fair amount of center field.

He’ll likely be a right-handed bat off the bench, occasional DH and fill in at various positions.

Ten Arizona football players have been named to the Shriner’s Children’s East West bowl watch list. Four offensive players and six defensive players are part of the 1,000-player list that ranges from all four levels of college football.

🔟 Wildcats land on the 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟳 𝗦𝗵𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗕𝗼𝘄𝗹 𝟭𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝗪𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵 𝗟𝗶𝘀𝘁‼️ pic.twitter.com/4TuRv0S5fu

— Arizona Football (@ArizonaFBall) July 23, 2026

The four players on offense include quarterback Noah Fifita, offensive linemen Tristan Bounds and Alexander Doost, and wide receiver Tre Spivey. The six players on defense include defensive linemen Tre Smith and Leroy Palu, linebackers Taye Brown, Chase Kennedy, and Everett Roussaw Jr., and cornerback Jay’Vion Cole.

Fifita returns for one final season in Tucson after throwing for 3,228 yards and 29 touchdowns. He has also been named to the preseason all-Big 12 team and Allstate AFCA Good Works Team.

Bounds’ final season was supposed to be last season, but after a season ending injury, he was granted an extra year of eligibility. He will be playing right next to Doost protecting Fifita’s right side.

Spivey was the ultimate play maker from last season’s offense. He had 381 receiving yards and seven touchdowns, and also had one rushing touchdown. Two of his touchdowns came from 70 and 57 yards.

Similar to Bounds, what was supposed to be Smith’s final season at Arizona was cut short due to injury. After being granted an extra year of eligibility, he is looking to make an impact on the defensive front in his final ride with the Wildcats.

Also along the defensive front, Palu will also be entering his final season in Tucson. Last season, he had 28 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, and a fumble recovery.

The trio of Brown, Kennedy, and Roussaw Jr. are all entering their final seasons with Arizona. Brown had 93 tackles, 12.5 tackles for loss, a fumble recovery and interception last season. Kennedy had 42 tackles, eight tackles for loss, four sacks, and two forced fumbles last season.

Roussaw Jr. transferred in from Memphis where he had 64 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, two forced fumbles and an interception. Cole returns as the leader of the Wildcats’ secondary and was a key contributor to team 122 last season.

He had 23 tackles, three tackles for loss, a sack and forced fumble. Cole’s most noticeable stat is the four interceptions that he had, including one he took back for a touchdown against Weber State.

The nominations for the 10 Wildcats add onto the excitement building for training camp and the season opener against NAU on Sept. 5.

title: Should UNC leave the ACC if offered?
description: There are no sports right now, so let’s revisit social media’s most toxic topic.
fullText:
Congress is in the process of trying to solve the problems that the NCAA refuses to fix — leveling the NIL/transfer portal playing field, and figuring how to navigate realignment. Focusing on realignment specifically, one of the options on the table is capping the Big Ten and SEC to a certain amount of schools per conference, and there’s also been a lot of talk about the SEC leaving the NCAA as a whole.

Because, you know, the SEC is too good than to stay in the asylum anymore (sarcasm).

When it comes to the ACC, nobody really knows what the future will hold, but there’s been whispers for years that UNC is a potential target for one of the bigger two conferences and that the school is interested. Here’s the thing: it’s probably been discussed, but the Grant of Rights has become such an issue for any school even thinking about leaving that it’s probably not even worth the conversation, especially now that programs are bleeding money due to revenue sharing with their players. Is that to say UNC couldn’t figure it out? Not necessarily, but it would be a very hard thing to pull off, and I have a feeling they would have to get donors onboard as well.

That said, let’s have some fun and discuss a hypothetical anyway. Let’s say money isn’t an issue to Carolina, they are more than willing to buy their way out of the Grant of Rights, and they begin seriously considering next steps. Would you want them to head to the Big Ten or SEC? Or would you want them to stay in the ACC? There’s good arguments for both sides of this conversation, but ultimately what it comes down to is money vs. tradition. UNC would undoubtedly pull in more money in another conference, but would it be worth losing some of their soul?

Let us know what you would want UNC to do in the comments below.

title: Chicago Bears 2026 Training Camp Position Breakdown: Cornerback
description: Next up in his position-by-position series, @wiltfongjr previews the Bears' cornerbacks.
fullText:
Last season, the Chicago Bears had three cornerbacks spend all of, or most of, the year on injured reserve. Two of those players appear to be back and ready to go for training camp, Jaylon Johnson and Terell Smith, but the third, Kyler Gordon, has missed time this offseason with what was reported to be a soft tissue injury.

There’s no question the Bears are better with Gordon on the field. His versatility opens things up for Dennis Allen, which is why he was paid so handsomely before the 2025 season. But missing so many games last year and now missing time during the offseason workouts must have head coach Ben Johnson a bit miffed.

“This spring was going to be a springboard for us to get going in the right direction,” Johnson said last month via the Chicago Sun-Times. “So, you know, we’re still working through that. We’re still trying to get that availability piece going. We know he’s a good player when he’s out there, but trust level is a huge thing for this team, for this coaching staff, for the locker room, and you can only develop that trust by being available.”

Gordon’s deal runs through the 2028 season, and contractually, the Bears would take a big dead cap hit if they moved on before that season, so they need him to get right and be one of the best nickels in the game for at least the next two years.

Jaylon Johnson was slowed a bit during the offseason, but earlier this month, in a social media post, his foot specialist declared him to be 100%.

Tyrique Stevenson is probably the odds-on favorite to start at corner opposite Jaylon, but he needs to be more consistent. The flashes have always been there — in 45 games over 3 years, he has 7 interceptions (1 TD), 38 passes defended, 5 forced fumbles, 2 fumble recoveries, and 3 tackles for loss — but it’s the lapses between the flashes that have been the issue, so hopefully that’s in the past.

“The young man that reported last year is so totally different than the young man that’s reporting this year,” Stevenson’s position coach, Al Harris, recently said about him. “He’s focused in, he’s locked in.”

Stevenson’s main competition could be fourth-round pick Malik Muhammad, but don’t be surprised if Muhammad is also working out at nickel.

Josh Blackwell has been a core special teamer for Richard Hightower’s third phase since 2022.

The Bears ended the 2025 season with eight cornerbacks on the 53-man roster, and they opened up week one with six of them. Cam Lewis, whom I mentioned with the safeties, has nickel experience and could factor into the depth of this position group.

Since being a UDFA in 2022, Jaylon Jones has 6 starts across 56 games played for the Bears, and his ability to play outside, nickel, and special teams will likely find him back in Chicago.

Terell Smith also shared a workout video earlier this month and looks to be good to go. He was drafted for the previous zone-based scheme, so we’ll need to see how he fits into Allen’s defense. I like his physicality, so if he can press, redirect, and recover, he should make the team.

Dallis Flowers was on the Bears’ practice squad last year, and he was active for a game. In his 4-year career, he has appeared in 24 games with 5 starts.

Dontae Manning was also on the Bears’ practice squad a year ago.

Chicago has one UDFA corner on the roster this offseason, KC Eziomume from Tulane. His 4.38 forty at his pro day likely turned some heads.

How many corners do you think they open the 2026 season with?

title: Will Tyler Kinley make it to the end of the season?
description: I went a whole Kinley post and didn’t even mention the William McKinley thing
fullText:
Tyler Kinley’s relationship to the Braves has been an odd one over the last year.

Before 2025, Kinley had a career 107/102/109 line (ERA-/FIP-/xFIP-) and 1.2 fWAR in just under 260 innings. Most of that value was accrued in 2022, when his season was cut short by injury. It’s also important to keep in mind that there’s at least some evidence that the Coors Field park effects are overly punishing to hitters and therefore overly generous to pitchers.

Before the Braves traded for him in 2025, it was more of the same: 118/96/113. Those numbers are barely rosterable for a reliever aside from a low HR/FB. The Braves hoped they could get more out of him, and they did in some ways, though it wasn’t exactly him hitting a new gear or anything: 17/68/105. Basically, Kinley had an epic run of not having runs charged to him and allowing very homers… while pitching as effectively (or, I guess, ineffectively) like the Kinley of old. The Braves had Kinley throw fewer fastballs, work harder on getting the fastball up, and change the way he threw his curveball so that it came out of a similar arm slot as his slider. They had him focus on getting the breaking pitches in the zone, with the fastball going above it.

Kinley did all of this. There is a very clear breakpoint in his pitch usage and location, among other things, between his time with the Braves and the Rockies. This wasn’t a matter of an inability to implement desired changes. It was just that it didn’t really matter. Though Kinley did halve his walk rate as a result of the changes, getting the ball in the zone or higher made him less of a grounder-generator and didn’t help him in the strikeout department. The fewer walks were great, but that was largely the only benefit.

While we don’t know the reasons, all of this led to a surprising-at-the-time-I-guess? declining of his team option in the offseason. There was some clamor about $5.5 million being an okay price for Kinley’s services, but from my perspective, there was no reason to give a reliever who never pitched all that well and couldn’t even manage a 100 xFIP- with the Braves anything above league minimum in the first place. The Braves ultimately re-signed Kinley for $4.25 million, essentially saving $1.25 million relative to his option price.

There was a stretch, a relatively brief one, where Kinley at least seemed better. Through May 3, he kind of seemed like he was picking up where he left off in 2025, with a little bit better performance overall: 42/82/94. His walk rate was back up to its former gross levels, but he was actually striking a bit more guys out. A reliever with an xFIP- around 90, especially one that you believe has some contact/homer suppression, can definitely play in a bullpen.

It didn’t last, though. Over the next month or so, Kinley went 111/130/96. His walk rate fell, but so did the grounder rate. You can write off the homers, as well, HR/FB stuff, but it didn’t feel great. His elbow may not have felt great, either, as he missed about a few weeks with inflammation.

At this point, Kinley has been back for about a month, and his performance has been ghastly. 231/202/132 is really bad. His strikeout rate plummeted, his walk rate is bad again, he’s barely getting any grounders. Joel Payamps got canned after a 193/137/116 line. Aaron Bummer got canned after a 179/207/136 line. The Braves ate some money in both of those cases. Kinley could very well be next: his season line is now 107/125/103, and has been getting dramatically worse basically every other outing or so.

Probably the biggest issue is that in aggregate, Kinley is losing any reason for positive prognosis. Even if he was never a guy to dream on given his track record, you could at least… ponder that he’d be okay for a while? But, with his season xFIP- crossing the 100 mark again, and with him not even doing the homer suppression thing, there’s not much there there. Basically every plate discipline metric is down across the board from his Braves stint in 2025, and his fastball command has been an utter disaster. While he’s really honed his slider release such that it hits the corner of the zone over and over, that’s actually not as helpful when everyone knows it’s coming at least two out of every three pitches, and he has no idea where his fastball is going. (The fact that the slider’s shape isn’t very good is another detriment — batters have an easier time hitting it relative to another slider if they know it’s coming and they can reach it, and they definitely know it’s coming and can reach it in the zone.)

So, put all that together, consider the impending Trade Deadline, and… will Tyler Kinley make it to season’s end with the Braves? Or, will they eat another partial reliever salary to reconfigure their bullpen to hopefully be a bit better?

title: Simple rule could’ve saved Charley Hull three shots after putting off the green at the Scottish Open
description: Charley Hull’s opening round at the ISPS HANDA Women’s Scottish Open was one to forget. Hull carded a round of six-over par 78 on Thursday at the Women’s Scottish Open.
fullText:
Charley Hull’s opening round at the ISPS HANDA Women’s Scottish Open was one to forget.

Hull carded a round of six-over par 78 on Thursday at the Women’s Scottish Open.

The Englishwoman played fairly average golf on the whole at Dundonald Links, but her round completely unravelled very early on.

Charley Hull made three bogeys, a solitary birdie and a seriously damaging quadruple bogey nine on the par-five fifth hole during her opening round.

Her round of 78 put her a whopping 12 shots adrift of the leader Jenny Shin after one round at the Women’s Scottish Open.

The good news for Hull is that she is currently just one stroke adrift of the cutline as she heads out for her second at Dundonald Links.

However, things could have been a lot brighter for Hull, had she taken advantage of one little-known rule.

Hull has made a bad habit out of getting off to slow starts in the big events on the LPGA Tour this season.

And that trend continued at the Women’s Scottish Open as she carded a score of 78.

However, had she thought on her feet, Hull could have saved herself three strokes, or two at worst.

Rule 18.1 on the USGA’s list of rules and regulations stipulates that ‘Relief under penalty of stroke and distance is allowed at any time’.

As the rule states, stroke and distance can be taken at ‘any time’, and anywhere on the golf course.

That means that, yes, golfers can take stroke and distance on the greens as well.

The rule is certainly not commonly known even at the highest level of the game, but it can save golfers numerous strokes.

Had Hull been aware of the rule, or thought quicker after putting her birdie attempt off the green, she could have taken stroke and distance relief.

Then, she would have been faced with exactly the same putt for a bogey. It’s also worth noting that Hull would have been given a free read after making her first attempt.

If she took two putts after taking stroke and relief, she would have made a double bogey seven.

However, had she holed the putt, she would have made a six – three strokes better than the nine that she eventually carded.

The crazy thing is that after taking stroke and distance relief, Hull’s putt for bogey would have been much more desirable than the ridiculously difficult chip that she left herself down below the surface of the green.

The Englishwoman took a further five strokes to get her ball in the hole after she putted off the green.

Hopefully Charley Hull is now aware of rule 18.1a, because it could save her strokes in the future.

Even if she had two-putted for a double bogey after taking stroke and distance relief, her 78 would have become a 76, and that could have made all the difference come the end of the week.

title: Who is the Phillies prospect most likely to be moved at the trade deadline?
description: There’s not many, but some will go
fullText:
We’ve all seen the latest prospect rankings that cast the Phillies farm system in a rather dim light. We all know that they don’t have much in the way of ammunition to acquire upgrades at this upcoming trade deadline.

But that doesn’t mean they won’t be sending any of their prospects out in a deal over the next week and some change. Dave Dombrowski likely won’t be shopping in the Jhoan Duran tier of the market as he did a year ago, but Dombrowski and the Phillies are certain to be heavily involved in the Harrison Bader tier of the market to put it in 2025 terms. They will likely be targeting rentals which of course come with less cost in prospect capital than players with multiple years of control.

It can’t be ruled out that the likes of Gage Wood or Aidan Miller could be moved, but it feels extremely unlikely, especially in Miller’s case due to injury. Once you get into the Ramon Marquez, Dante Nori, and Aroon Escobar tier of the Phillies system though, it’s extremely likely that at least a couple of players will be moved. Again, there’s not much in the way of trade bait for a big fish, but there’s enough to find moderate upgrades if the opportunity cost is weighed correctly. The Phillies have enough glaring holes that even a mid-tier upgrade could go a long way to increasing their win total and therefore their chances at the division title or the postseason in general.

So, who is the Phillies prospect most likely to be moved at the deadline? Does your prediction align with what you would do if you were in charge of the deadline?

title: Friday Cheese Curds: Packers will look for answers on both lines in training camp
description: The offensive line in particular needs to answer the call after moving so many parts around this offseason.
fullText:
We’re now just days away from the opening of the Green Bay Packers’ 2026 training camp. It has been a long offseason, but the pads will finally go on next week, with the team’s first practice set for next Wednesday, July 29.

Over the following five weeks or so, the Packers will need to settle on a roster, but also on the final roles across their offensive and defensive lines. Those two units both face significant questions this summer, but the questions are very different depending on which side of the football you’re on.

Defensively, it’s all about determining a hierarchy on the edge and a plan for how to line up on the interior. With Micah Parsons likely to miss at least the first four games of the regular season for his ACL rehab, the need to assemble a passable pass rush is critical. Lukas Van Ness will lead that charge, but who will step up behind him? Rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton should have plenty of opportunities in camp to show that he deserves snaps early on as a rookie — and that his draft weekend slide to the 4th round was indeed a mistake by much of the NFL. The interior line’s questions instead focus around who will play what position — namely nose tackle when the team lines up with a 3-man front.

On the offensive line, the questions are less about who plays where and more around whether the expected starters at several positions are ready for the big time. Only two spots on the line have the same likely starter as at the start of last season, with Aaron Banks at left guard and Zach Tom at right tackle. Otherwise, Jordan Morgan takes over at left tackle, Sean Rhyan has moved to center, and Anthony Belton likely gets the call at guard, rather than playing tackle as he did early last season.

Can that unit gel in training camp, stay healthy, and become a consistent reliable unit? The Packers certainly hope they can answer in the affirmative over the course of the 2026 season.

One Packers Rookie With Best Chance to Surprise Everyone (And Sack History) | SI.com
If Dani Dennis-Sutton beats historical trends to become a sack machine in his rookie year despite being a day-three draft pick, it won’t surprise everyone — especially not most of us here at APC.

Countdown to camp: Jordan Morgan takes over Packers’ blind side | Packers.com
It’s about time. Frankly, after seeing how he played at tackle towards the end of the 2025 season, it’s a bit frustrating that he didn’t end up starting over Rasheed Walker last year.

OL expert ranks Packers OL as 29th best in NFL entering 2026 | Packers Wire
Given the Packers’ success in developing linemen over the years, it’s reasonable for fans to have a knee-jerk reaction to reject this analysis. Still, there are questions at multiple positions that need to be settled, with several players (including the aforementioned Morgan) lining up in different spots from where they played in much of 2025.

LISTEN: 2026 Opponent Preview: Green Bay Packers | Bears Talk Underground
Tex joins Larry Dyer for a quick look back at the Packers’ 2025 and a more lengthy preview of what to expect from Green Bay in the upcoming season.

Ed Policy to preside over his first Packers shareholders meeting July 27 | Packersnews.com
Who’s planning on going to the meeting on Monday? If you are, be ready for warm weather and a chance of scattered storms.

Man tossed by Yellowstone bison says hitting the ground was the worst part | ABC News
Well as the saying goes: it’s not the fall, it’s the landing.

title: Sophie Cunningham’s Unlikely Path to WNBA Stardom
description: The reserve guard has become one of the WNBA’s most famous players.
fullText:
In the 30 days since Sophie Cunningham directed a prolonged point at DeWanna Bonner—and became a viral meme in the process—the Indiana Fever guard has gained more than a million followers on both Instagram and TikTok, according to digital analytics firm Social Blade.

For comparison, fellow Fever guard and WNBA megastar Caitlin Clark gained roughly 160,000 followers on Instagram during the same period. Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers and Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese—other faces of the league—gained approximately 8,500 and lost around 3,000, respectively.

Though Cunningham’s freshly supercharged Instagram follower count of 2.6 million is still well behind that of Clark (3.8 million), Bueckers (3 million) and Reese (5.2 million), her engagement rate—a metric of utmost importance to advertisers and brand partners—is much higher. Per Social Blade, Cunningham averages approximately 300,000 likes and 3,000 comments per post on the platform; Bueckers’s typical engagement—235,000 likes and 1,000 comments a post—is the next closest.

This isn’t Cunningham’s first surge since joining the Fever last year.

The guard—who had a relatively low profile during her six previous seasons with the Phoenix Mercury—earned a reputation as Caitlin Clark’s “enforcer” after getting into a brawl with then-Connecticut Sun guard Jacy Sheldon during a June 2025 Commissioner’s Cup game. Shortly after the incident, Cunningham launched a podcast with Colin Cowherd’s digital media network, The Volume. (The podcast, called Show Me Something, is co-hosted by Cunningham’s high school classmate West Wilson, formerly of Bravo’s Summer House.)

While she experienced roughly equal follower growth after her enforcer moment last summer, the jump only propelled her to semi-mainstream status. In contrast, this latest spike places Cunningham firmly among the WNBA’s most-followed players on Instagram, passing up established stars such as A’ja Wilson (1.5 million) and Sabrina Ionescu (1.4 million), as well as young, digital-native talent like Flau’jae Johnson (2 million) and Cameron Brink (1.3 million).

General interest is much higher this time around, too: ESPN published a 4,000-word profile on Cunningham earlier this week, and searches for “Sophie Cunningham” are up 130% year-over-year, according to Google Trends data. Two of the five best-selling jerseys on the WNBA’s official storefront, meanwhile, currently belong to Cunningham.

It all begs a big question: How will the eighth-year guard, who has a career average of 8.0 points per game, personally capitalize on this next-level notoriety?

The most immediate and obvious answer is to push merchandise tied to her viral finger-point, which she is free to do as long as no official league logos or branding are used. (Earlier this week, a WNBPA spokesperson told Front Office Sports that it prohibits its dozens of official licensee partners from monetizing any moments involving confrontation between players.)

A representative for Cunningham did not immediately respond to a request for comment about her plans to launch any products, pointing meme-related or otherwise. But the guard’s recent side quests suggest she has serious show business ambitions.

After making her Sports Illustrated Swimsuit debut in May, Cunningham took up another modeling role as a ring girl at UFC 329 in Las Vegas on July 11. In a post-fight press conference, UFC president Dana White revealed the stint was not pre-planned, but happened organically thanks to the “relationship” the two have “created.” (Cunningham was in town with the Fever to play the Aces the next day.) Still, her ringside interest isn’t totally random; in a December 2025 episode of her podcast, she expressed a desire to one day join WWE.

Cunningham also joined USA Network as a WNBA contributor and part-time studio analyst this season—a role that a handful of her peers have since taken on with other platforms.

Her newfound ubiquity, however, has also fueled polarization. On multiple occasions over the last month, official Trump administration X accounts have shared images and videos of the pointing meme without any pushback from Cunningham, which some social media users view as her endorsing a MAGA worldview.

In her ESPN profile, Cunningham described her politics as “very much in the middle,” but did make her stance on trans athlete participation known: “I want to protect young girls in a locker room,” Cunningham told writer Hallie Grossman, “or young girls in a sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.” Speaking to reporters in Indianapolis after the profile was published, the former Missouri star doubled down on her stance.

Taking to Instagram on Thursday, she seemingly tripled down: “I said what I said,” she captioned a post of her doing a pregame walk.

Cunningham’s comments sparked backlash.

Them’s Quispe López noted that, even though brief, her wording contained “multiple anti-trans dog whistles,” including the language of “protection.” High Post Hoops’s Stephanie Kaloi wrote: “The phrase ’biological men’ or ’biological women’ in this context is often used in a way that is derogatory and, frankly, mean,” adding that Cunningham’s comments “at best, indicate a lack of understanding about the health and lives of transgender girls and women, and they also support an ideology that is considered transphobic by many allies and members of the LGBTQ+ community.”

Still, the criticism hasn’t done much to slow her social media skyrocket: In the two days since the article was published, Cunningham has netted roughly 50,000 new followers on Instagram and 100,000 on TikTok, once again according to Social Blade data. (The comments also earned her a high-profile supporter in Stephen A. Smith, who defended her stance on his SiriusXM show Thursday afternoon.)

The only area where Cunningham seems immune to constant growth—at least as of late—is her Show Me Something podcast co-hosted by now-ex-Summer House cast member Wilson, who left the popular Bravo TV show earlier this year after a romantic scandal. The podcast averages between 10,000 and 60,000 views per show on YouTube, and has yet to notch more than 50,000 listens on a single of its 48 episodes on Spotify.

The specific terms of Cunningham and West’s deal with The Volume are unknown. The media network could not immediately be reached for comment about long-term plans for the show or its intentions to retain Cunningham as a talent.

Nevertheless, Cunningham’s 12-month rise from solid but unspectacular bench player to one of the WNBA’s most famous figures is remarkable. If she benefited from an association with Clark last summer, this summer Cunningham has created a presence entirely her own—one that is poised to prove lucrative no matter her on-court circumstances.

Case in point: As the basketball world descends upon Chicago for the WNBA’s 2026 All-Star Weekend, Cunningham—who is averaging a respectable 9.3 points in 22.9 minutes per game this season—won’t be participating in the exhibition. But she will be nearby in Romeoville, Illinois, on Friday, July 24, to promote the launch of her first player-exclusive shoe with Adidas.

The post Sophie Cunningham’s Unlikely Path to WNBA Stardom appeared first on Front Office Sports.

title: Bogdan Guskov offers hilarious prediction for ‘big chance’ against Magomed Ankalaev at UFC Abu Dhabi
description: Bogdan Guskov was originally scheduled to face Jan Blachowicz in a rematch at UFC Belgrade
fullText:
Bogdan Guskov didn’t waste any time putting a rematch with Jan Blachowicz on the back burner to face Magomed Ankalaev at UFC Abu Dhabi.

Guskov heads to his first main event against the former champion at Saturday’s Fight Night card — which is a week earlier than he was slated to compete against Blachowicz at UFC Belgrade after fighting to a majority draw at UFC 323 this past December.

Not only did Guskov see it as an opportunity to advance even higher in the rankings, but he believes he’s getting a shot at a much bigger face in the UFC.

“Yes, because I [look at] this fight like [a big] chance,” Guskov told MMA Fighting. “This chance can change my career, change my life, and this Ankalaev, I think [he has bigger] name than Jan. I [didn’t] need to think a lot of time because UFC after when [asking about a] fight, everybody say, ‘Oh I say yes, I say no, I am safe for me to go to scale, I need to go to another country, [to] another planet.’

“For me, [didn’t] need time for me to say, ‘Hey, let’s go.’ I say let’s go like this, 50 seconds.”

Guskov is unbeaten in his past five fights after dropping his debut to Volkan Oezdemir in September 2023. “Hitman” has finished all four of his octagon victories, including wins over Ryan Spann and Nikita Krylov.

With Ankalaev returning for the first time since losing the light heavyweight title to Alex Pereira at UFC 320 this past October, which Guskov called simply “a bad day at the office” for Ankalaev, and with new champ Carlos Ulberg on the sidelines following his title win over Jiri Prochazka at April’s UFC 327 event, Guskov sees this fight as a massive opportunity.

“Carlos have an injury now,” Guskov said. “Maybe after this win, maybe give another opponent. For me, it doesn’t matter who, but just chance for a fight chance for a fight [for] interim title.”

As far as a prediction goes, Guskov is as loosey-goosey as can be.

“My fights, every time is like Walido. You know what Walido is? Aspirin,” Guskov said. “Be ready, take a pillow, and eat this one. My fights every time is like this. This is it.

“I love this one because [I fight] every time with emotion. I think on this, this fight is the same.”

title: Cowboys O-line: Pressure from the edges, stability from the inside
description: Dallas doesn't have an offensive line problem. It has an edge protection problem.
fullText:
The Cowboys don’t have an offensive line problem. They have an edge protection problem.

The data from 2025 makes that distinction surprisingly clear. While both tackle spots allowed well above-average pressure, Dallas’ three interior starters quietly performed at or above the NFL average.

Today, we look at how the Cowboys linemen compared against the NFL average in 2025, how many splash plays (sacks + hits + hurries) they gave up, and what that could mean for 2026. The numbers we’re going to use are from Pro Football Focus (PFF), but we’re only looking at their raw stats, not the grades. Importantly, the PFF numbers can differ from the official totals because PFF only lists splash plays that are directly attributable to an offensive line player.

But before we start comparing sacks, hits, and hurries among players along the offensive line, it’s important to understand that you can’t compare players without also accounting for their snap count, because one guy may have played 450 pass blocking snaps, while the other guy played 650 snaps.

Example: Tyler Guyton gave up 31 total pressures (sacks + hits + hurries) according to PFF. Buffalo’s Pro Bowl left tackle Dion Dawkins gave up 33 pressures. If you’re a proponent of volume stats, you would argue that both gave up almost the same amount of pressures. Technically, you’d be right, but Guyton reached his total in just 384 pass-blocking snaps, while Dawkins played 528. Once you account for workload, the comparison looks very different.

To make every player directly comparable, I’ve normalized all pressure statistics to 600 pass-blocking snaps, roughly a full season for an NFL starter.

Here’s how many sacks, hits, and pressures an average NFL O-line gave up in 2025, adjusted to 600 pass-blocking snaps.

2025 NFL average splash plays given up by O-line (adjusted)

One interesting takeaway is that right tackles now allow almost as much pressure as left tackles. Whether that’s because elite edge rushers line up on both sides or offenses have become more balanced, the traditional blind-side gap has largely disappeared.

Now that we’ve established the baseline, or ‘average’ for these splash plays, let’s have a look at how the Cowboys five starting linemen compare. Note on the color scheme: green is better than the NFL average at the position, yellow is up to 25% below the NFL average, red is more than 25% worse than the NFL average.

body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 4px 6px !important; }

2025 splash plays given up by Cowboys O-line (adjusted)

When comparing each starter’s pass protection to the 2025 league average at his position, a clear pattern emerges: Dallas doesn’t have an offensive line problem. It has an edge protection problem.

Three starters are already performing at or above league average. The interior of the offensive line has already become one of the strengths of the roster.

Tyler Smith (LG) continues to perform at a high level, allowing about 8% fewer total pressures than the average NFL left guard.

Cooper Beebe (C) is almost exactly league average in total pressures allowed. While his QB hit rate is slightly elevated, he developed into a dependable center in just his second season, though you’d still like to see a little more green in his profile.

The biggest surprise may be rookie Tyler Booker (RG). Booker allowed fewer sacks than the average right guard, fewer QB hurries and 12% fewer total pressures than the league average. For a rookie stepping into the starting lineup, that’s an outstanding start.

Collectively, Dallas’ three interior starters are performing at, or slightly above, the NFL average. In fact, the three interior positions collectively rank 11th across the NFL in total adjusted pressures and 13th in adjusted sacks.

At left tackle, Tyler Guyton allowed 48.4 total adjusted pressures, compared to a league average of 39.8. That’s roughly 22% more pressure than the average NFL left tackle. At right tackle, Terence Steele allowed 47.0 adjusted pressures against a positional average of 34.4, nearly 37% above league average.

Viewed as a unit, the offensive line appears inconsistent. Viewed by position, the interior trio is providing reliable pass protection while the tackles are giving up the majority of the pressure. That distinction matters because it changes the conversation. Instead of saying “the offensive line needs to improve,” it’s more accurate to say “the tackles need to improve.”

Those are very different problems. One suggests rebuilding. The other suggests targeted development or a free-agent addition. Because the depth at tackle? O.M.G.!

body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 4px 6px !important; }

2025 splash plays given up by Cowboys backups (adjusted)

I’ve included the snap counts here because they are quite low and as a result, bad performances are hyper-magnified when adjusted to 600 snaps. Nevertheless, the issue remains that the problems last year were mostly at the edge.

Brock Hoffman’s numbers suggest he can survive as a backup, but they don’t suggest Dallas would have been comfortable if he had to start for an extended period, so he was allowed to leave for Pittsburgh.

T.J. Bass, on the other hand, has been been solid in limited opportunities at both guard spots, and with a little additional development he could be the interior swing guy.

But the tackle depth remains a real concern. Nate Thomas’ numbers came in a very small sample, making them difficult to evaluate, but they certainly don’t suggest a player ready to contribute meaningful snaps at tackle. The Cowboys would be well-advised to look for a swing tackle on the free agent market.

Again, the weakness isn’t spread evenly across the line. It’s concentrated at tackle.

The irony is that Dallas’ best pass-protecting tackle may already be on the roster. Tyler Smith’s brief stint at left tackle produced pressure numbers that would have ranked fifth among NFL starters. By comparison, his excellent left guard play ranked “only” ninth. Moving him back outside would weaken one position while dramatically strengthening another—a trade-off the Cowboys may eventually have to consider if Guyton doesn’t develop.

The Cowboys’ offensive line is not a five-man question mark. Three of the five starters are already performing at or above league average in pass protection. The challenge now is fixing the outside.

If Tyler Guyton takes the expected Year 3 leap, the perception of Dallas’ offensive line could change dramatically, not because the unit suddenly became good, but because its biggest weakness finally caught up with the majority of the line.

If he doesn’t, the Cowboys may already have the answer on the roster. Moving Smith back outside would weaken one position while potentially solving another, making it a difficult, but increasingly realistic, decision.

One way or another, the Cowboys don’t need to rebuild their entire offensive line. They need to solve the edges.

title: What’s the Shooting Stars competition, and which team will win this WNBA All-Star 2026 event?
description: The WNBA Shooting Stars competition will celebrate the past, present and future of the sport.
fullText:
The WNBA is always looking to mix things up during All-Star weekend to keep things fresh.

This year, the league is tossing the Skills Challenge and is implementing Shooting Stars in its place for Friday’s WNBA All-Star 2026 festivities (8 p.m. ET, ESPN).

Here’s what you need to know about the competition, as well as who might win. In the comments, tells us which team you think will shoot for the stars.

Shooting Stars will be a four-team competition.

Each team will represent a city, and the quartet selected is Minnesota, Seattle, Washington, and Dallas/Detroit. Detroit and Dallas are combined to recognize both the current Wings and the original Shock.

This competition will not only celebrate these regions, but also the past, present, and future of the WNBA.

🌟 KIA SHOOTING STARS EXPLAINED 🌟

Take a look through the @Kia Shooting Stars format ahead of WNBA All-Star Friday Night, tomorrow at 8pm/ET on ESPN! pic.twitter.com/qy3w70yyI3

The WNBA Shooting Stars competition is a two-round, timed shooting competition. Each team will have 70 seconds to score as many points as possible by shooting from seven locations around the court. They must shoot in order, starting at one and ending at the seventh location.

The two teams posting the highest scores in the opening round advance to the championship. In the last round, the team that scored the lowest of the two still standing will shoot first. Just like the first round, the winner will be whoever scores the most.

Each team will have a legend, a rising star and a standout high school player from Nike EYBL.

Elena Delle Donne (Washington Mystics)

Rebekkah Brunson (Minnesota Lynx)

The current WNBA players involved are:

Shakira Austin (Washington Mystics)

Flau’jae Johnson (Seattle Storm)

Courtney Williams (Minnesota Lynx)

The Nike EYBL players have not officially been assigned a team, but the players will be Jezelle Banks, Ryan Carter, Tatianna Griffin and Morghan Reckley.

The honorary general managers, Cynthia Cooper and Teresa Weatherspoon, will serve as designated passers. They will split the duties, with each passing to two different teams.

When trying to pick a winner, the biggest question mark is the legends.

Which ones are still shooters? Who will catch a rhythm and get hot? I think the team with the legend who is ready to hoop will be the one that wins the contest. Although, the Nike EYBL players are also X-factors. They’ve played in high-pressure games in high school and with Team USA competitions, but this is a big stage and not a traditional game.

All the teams have a great chance, but watch out for Washington. I’m confident that Delle Donne can still shoot, and Austin is a force as well.

title: Ranking the Denver Broncos’ defensive position groups prior to training camp
description: The Denver Broncos have one of the best defenses in the National Football League. How would you rank their position groups?
fullText:
Over the past two seasons, the Denver Broncos have sported one of the best defenses in the National Football League. Under the leadership of Vance Joseph, the team has embarked on a significant turnaround since his first year back leading the defense in 2023. They’ve led the NFL and posted franchise record breaking sack numbers in back-to-back years.

In order to achieve their goal of earning a fourth Lombardi Trophy, the defense is going to have to perform impeccably again this season. Leading up to training camp, here is my ranking of the Broncos’ defensive position groups. Feel free to offer your rankings and reasoning in the comments section.

The Broncos boast the best slate of corners in the NFL. I don’t believe that’s debatable. In fact, I bet every team wishes they had a starting trio of cornerbacks like Denver possesses.

Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja’Quan McMillian are head and shoulders above the competition. That formidable trio is set to lead the way at the position once again in 2026. After them, Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron are good players who would easily start for most any other franchise.

They do a fantastic job at limiting big plays down the field. Denver’s cornerback prowess was a big reason why they ranked second in the NFL in completion percentage and yards per attempt. They tied for fifth in touchdowns allowed and ranked seventh-best in yards per game.

While there were several pick-sixes by the group in ‘25, Denver’s defense only had 10 interceptions for the entire season. That’s something I’m optimistic will change for their upcoming ‘26 gridiron campaign. In fact, I believe they have ability to be one of the best in the league this season if they live up to their potential.

Denver’s group of edge rushers are definitely a big strength. They are a huge reason why the defense was able to put up eye-popping sack totals in ‘24 and ‘25. However, I have them just a smidge behind the cornerbacks in the overall positional group rankings.

There is no doubt fifth-year pro Nik Bonitto is the top player within the unit. After posting 27.5 sacks the past two seasons, Bonitto has earned two Pro-Bowl nods and is well on his way to an All-Pro honor in the future. His get-off at the line of scrimmage is amongst the league’s best. Moreover, his astounding 20-percent pressure rate is something Defensive Coordinator’s dream of with their edge rushers.

While I’m high the trio of Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman, the potential absence of Jonathon Cooper—at least for a portion of the season due to off the field issues—could become an issue. Cooper has been an underrated performer for the team. While his sack numbers waned down the stretch, his pressure rate of nearly 14-percent is Top 20 at the position.

Can Denver’s group of edge rushers pave the way for them to lead the league in sacks for a third straight season? I think so, but I wonder more if they have what it takes to get more sacks than they did last season. If so, that would be quite the accomplishment.

The departure of John Franklin-Myers to the Tennessee Titans is the main reason I have Denver’s defensive line group ranked third. Even with Franklin-Myers gone, they still have one top-tier performer at the position. Zach Allen is one of the team’s best players and one of the most underrated defensive trench players in the NFL. He’ll lead the way for the group upfront and is poised to have another dominant season.

Outside of Allen, I do like the depth they have. Nose tackle D.J. Jones has been a solid and reliable defender for the team since signing with them several seasons ago. Malcolm Roach was a good addition in last year’s free agent cycle. Fourth-year pro Eyioma Uwazurike could be a breakout candidate for the team this year and will be first in line to help offset the loss of Franklin-Myers.

The big question is how well and how much Sai’vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim will play this year. The franchise’s third round picks the past two drafts, both have tantalizing traits and pass rushing skills. But will they be able to flash enough in camp to show they are worthy of significant snaps this year? I can’t wait to find out.

I don’t consider the safety position to be a liability. It’s just that the three aforementioned positions have superior production, impact, and talent levels. Nevertheless, both Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga are quality starters and are certainly an underrated backend duo.

My big question is the depth behind them. In the event either Jones or Hufanga were to miss time, the Broncos would be banking on players with mostly special team’s experience to take over and start. However, potentially sliding Jahdae Barron back there could also be a part of the equation.

Devon Key is an All-Pro player on special teams. Boasting top-tier physical traits, JL Skinner has been a mainstay on special teams the past few years, but very little experience in games defensively. Tycen Anderson, the free agent signing from the Cincinnati Bengals, has virtually the same story as Skinner. Miles Scott was a ballhawk at Illinois, though is still a virtual unknown as a late-round rookie selection.

Your mileage may vary, but the position group on defense that concerns me the most is inside linebacker. It’s a shame the Dre Greenlaw experiment didn’t pan out. I was cautiously optimistic about the signing, but in the end, his inability to stay healthy was the primary culprit in his early exit from the Mile High City.

Given such, Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad will be the Broncos’ starting tandem on the inside. This was one area I thought they may have been aggressive in free agency upgrading. Yet continuity and knowledge of the defensive system meant a lot to the coaching staff and front office.

Outside of Singleton and Strnad, Denver’s group of inside linebackers doesn’t have a lot of NFL experience—especially when it comes to starting. Five players, most all of them UDFAs from the past several years, will be vying for several backup spots on the roster.

Jordan Turner, Levelle Bailey, Karene Reid, Red Murdock, and Taurean York will be in a fierce competition. That just might be the most heated position battle in all of training camp. These players won’t just be looking to prove themselves on special teams, they will be given the opportunity to show they have what it takes to start if called upon.

title: How Mizzou Can Navigate the Unknown at Right Tackle
description: With Josh Atkins out an extended period of time, what are Mizzou’s options to shore up right tackle
fullText:
One of the premium positions for Mizzou’s offense in 2026 is going to need some extended patchwork.

We knew earlier this spring that projected starting right tackle Josh Atkins would miss some time during the regular season due to injury. But at the top of the week, we learned that his absence would extend deeper into the season than originally projected.

Drinkwitz says #Mizzou Josh Atkins had a setback and the team isn’t as optimistic about a mid-season return

— Aaron Ladd (@aaronladdtv) July 20, 2026

Atkins transferred from Arizona State with over 2,000 career snaps at left tackle between the Sun Devils and Hawaii, but was projected to be a replacement for Keagan Trost, who was drafted to the Los Angeles Rams.

Right tackle is one of the most important positions entering 2026 as the Tigers have a left-handed quarterback in Austin Simmons, who has just 259 collegiate snaps. Drinkwitz noted the importance of the position earlier this week.

“Another player is our right tackle, whoever emerges,” Eli Drinkwitz said at SEC Media Days. “We got a lot of really good candidates, but that position is going to be important, just for the security of the offense.”

As mentioned above, Mizzou is entering this year with a void at right tackle, but options are available until, or if Atkins returns.

There’s a few candidates that can fill the right tackle position in 2026. At the SEC Media Day’s Drinkwitz highlighted a few names when talking about who could fill that role. I’ve separated these candidates into two different tiers. The first being the more experienced options, arrivals from Mississippi State, Zach Owens and Luke Work.

As for Owens, he is the most experienced portal addition outside of Atkins on the offensive line. In a full-time role with Mississippi State, he played 564 snaps (319 on the right, 200 on the left). The caveat is that this was at guard. He was recruited as a tackle, but there are plenty of differences when it comes to playing both positions in terms of timing, technique, etc. But this was something the Tigers had Cayden Green do not too long ago, and it worked out just fine.

It Owens moves to right tackle, it creates another issue because who would then go to the then vacant guard position as the configuration would look like this: Green-VOID-Guidice-Peagler-Owens. Moving Owens solves a more important issue, but then we would be discussing options at guard.

Work has been a more versatile player the past two seasons at Mississippi State, and is someone Drinkwitz highlighted at Media Days. He has collected snaps at every position on the offensive line aside from center, including 241 at left tackle, 145 at right tackle, 76 at left guard and 19 at right guard.

His snaps at right tackle came in 2024 against Mizzou and Mississippi where he received PFF grades of 63.5 and 46.3. Not ideal for what you want to see from the position, but his sample size is more than the younger alternatives.

Missouri has successfully recruited the tackle position well in-state under Drinkwitz. Armand Membou is a prime example, but recently that trend continued with:

Logan Reichert (2024). A former 3-star recruit who chose the Tigers over Oregon, Georgia, LSU, Michigan, and plenty of others.

Jack Lange (2025). A former 4-star who was the No. 1 player in Missouri coming out of high school.

Both have an extremely small sample size collegiately. Reichert played one snap at center against Arkansas in 2025 and 56 snaps at left guard in 2024. As for Lange, he played one snap against Louisiana in 2025.

With how highly both were recruited, Lange and Reichert offer a wide range of outcomes long-term. If Missouri elects to go younger at the position, it will give the team the data they need to see if these guys are ready to play earlier than anticipated.

There isn’t a clear right or wrong answer on what direction the team decides. They can go with options that have already seen high level play, or attempt to get the most out of their recruits now.

Not being naive to the situation, the Tigers have found themselves in, there will be growing pains with whoever plays at right tackle in 2026. Having Atkins at the position was supposed to be an immediate short-term fix at the position following Keagan Trosts’ departure to the NFL.

So, the next question is what can Missouri do to help mitigate potential disasters with a lesser experienced quarterback and players that are more inexperienced at the position?

Well, maintaining a run-first identity is key, and we shouldn’t expect the Tigers to shy away from that anytime soon. The Tigers have been one of the more run dominant rushing attacks in the SEC, and we do know Ahmad Hardy is 5-8 weeks from returning. It keeps the team out of clear passing situations and limits how often a tackle goes against pass rushes.

In the passing department quick game and RPOs are going to be important as well. I’ve spent the early parts of the summer saying how Mizzou needs to attack more vertically, they still will, but Atkins’ absence could make it more difficult. As for Austin Simmons in 2025, he had a 87.3 PFF offensive grade when the pocket was kept clean and 28.5 grade when under pressure. Two vastly different outcomes.

Simmons comes from a RPO system at Mississippi and also, Lindsey comes from a Michigan team that utilizes tight ends, meaning chipping will be key, and releasing some burden from whoever is at right tackle.

Losing one of the most important pieces on offense for an even larger extended period of time sucks, and there will be an impact. But the Tigers aren’t without answers. There are multiple options at right tackle, personnel-wise and schematically.

Owens and Work have experience, while Reichert and Lange provide upside. It will take a combination of someone stepping up and some scheme adjustments until, or if, Atkins returns.

title: LA Dodgers and MVP Ohtani launch summer of live baseball on BBC
description: World Series champions the Los Angeles Dodgers will launch a summer of live Major League Baseball on the BBC.
fullText:
Defending World Series champions the Los Angeles Dodgers will launch a summer of live Major League Baseball on the BBC when they meet the New York Mets on Sunday.

The Dodgers lead the National League again in 2026, with last season's Most Valuable Player, Shohei Ohtani, to the fore as they target a third consecutive World Series title.

The struggling Mets are in need of inspiration from star man Juan Soto as they look to turn around a difficult start to the season.

The game sets up a run of 10 consecutive live Sunday night MLB matches on the BBC, including the season finale on September 27 before four post-season games the following week.

Why Dodgers are on brink of World Series dynasty

The night the Tartan Army took over iconic Fenway Park

The Dodgers' record of 65 wins and 38 defeats means they are likely to win the National League West for the 13th time in 14th years.

Their recent dominance is built around Ohtani, whose achievements are now compared to the greatest players in the history of the game.

His ability to both hit and pitch at the top level consistently - he already has 22 home runs this year and has recorded eight wins as a pitcher - demonstrates a similar skill-set to the legendary two-way player Babe Ruth.

Ohtani has been named Most Valuable Player in his league four times, including last season, when the Dodgers became the first franchise in 25 years to win consecutive World Series titles.

Dominican left-fielder Soto became the highest-paid player in baseball history in 2024 when he left the New York Yankees and signed a $765m deal with their bitter cross-city rivals the Mets.

He hit his 250th career home run against the Yankees earlier this season, one of 21 home runs he has delivered in 2026.

Despite Soto's contribution, the Mets narrowly missed out on a post-season berth last year and now sit bottom of the National League East with 43 wins to 60 defeats.

This season, the MLB Bases Covered Live team will again be led by play-by-play announcer Melanie Newman, with former St Louis Cardinals first baseman Xavier Scruggs and Maccabees guitarist Felix White alongside to call the action for seasoned baseball fans and new viewers.

During the 2026 Fifa World Cup, baseball played an unexpectedly large role in the experiences of football fans and players from the UK as they enjoyed memorable outings to ballparks across the US.

After defeating Haiti in their opening game in nearby Foxborough, Scotland's Tartan Army took over Fenway Park in Boston to celebrate while watching the Red Sox take on the Texas Rangers.

England manager Thomas Tuchel threw out the first pitch at Kaufmann Stadium when several members of the England squad watched the Kansas City Royals play the St Louis Cardinals.
