title: Tyler Adams Explains Mauricio Pochettino’s Impact on USMNT
description: We discuss the World Cup awards and whether the right players received them.
fullText:
The biggest news that fans of the United States Men’s National Team are waiting for is the decision by current head coach Mauricio Pochettino. Will he accept the contract extension that U.S. Soccer offered before the start of the World Cup? That’s the question that U.S. Soccer hopes will be answered soon.

Midfielder Tyler Adams spoke with Stars & Stripes FC this week as part of his work with Allstate opening up a mini-pitch in Atlanta. He took the time during that interview to explain the impact Pochettino had on him and the rest of the USMNT.

“I’ve been very fortunate with the managers I’ve been able to work under and learn from. [How] Pochettino leads a group of people and the culture he leads with is so important,” Adams said. “Put the tactics and how he improved me as a player aside, how he improved me as a person, the intangibles and the culture he created was incredible.”

Pochettino led the USMNT to the Round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, setting a record for most USMNT wins at a single World Cup in the process. Since he took over as head coach in September 2024, he has a 17W-12L-2D record. During the World Cup, he had the team competing at their highest ability until it all fell apart in the Round of 16 against Belgium. Still, having a full cycle of Pochettino, despite the history with coaches getting a second cycle, could bring some continuity that the team hasn’t had in quite some time.

Pochettino has said that a decision on his future will come soon. Should he continue as coach, it seems like he will have a player pool that will fight for him as they attempt to build on the foundation they’ve set and keep fans engaged and supportive. World Cup qualifying begins next fall, but they have Concacaf Nations League as well as the 2027 Gold Cup before that. Pochettino’s decision will affect the team’s approach to those competitions.

title: Lazio Contact the Agent of Unsettled AC Milan Attacker
description: Lazio have reportedly made concrete steps in their attempts to sign Santiago Gimenez, who could be on his way out of AC Milan.Lazio’s Market OptionsThe Biancocelesti are determined to bolster their ...
fullText:
Lazio have reportedly made concrete steps in their attempts to sign Santiago Gimenez, who could be on his way out of AC Milan.

The Biancocelesti are determined to bolster their attacking ranks with a new centre-forward capable of guaranteeing goals. In recent weeks, they have linked with a plethora of candidates, especially Fluminense’s John Kennedy, Sassuolo’s Andrea Pinamonti, Fiorentina’s Roberto Piccoli, and Levante’s Carlos Espi.

Nevertheless, sources had long identified Gimenez as the club’s dream target. Earlier this week, it was reported that Lazio have rekindled their interest in the Mexican international.

According to La Lazio Siamo Noi, the Italian capital side made initial contact with Rafaela Pimenta, the famous Brazilian lawyer who represents Gimenez. The player is said to be enticed by the opportunity to join Lazio, while Milan could be open to offloading him after signing Goncalo Ramos from PSG.

Nevertheless, the Lazio management must find a creative formula, as they cannot afford to buy the Rossoneri striker outright. An initial loan deal remains the most likely option.

After rising through the ranks of Cruz Azul, the 25-year-old made a name for himself in Europe during his time at Feyenoord, bagging 65 goals in his 105 appearances for the Dutch club. In January 2025, he completed a €30 million transfer to Milan, but he has only netted seven times over the last 18 months. Therefore, Lazio would aim to restore the Rotterdam version of the player should he arrive at Formello.

title: Astros vs. White Sox Series Primer with White Sox Voice Len Kasper
description: Although lacking the drama of their historical post season battles, the three game series forthcoming on Chicago’s south side holds heightened significance should the Astros hope to remain relevant this baseball season. Len Kasper calls games for the White Sox and he joins us exclusively at The Crawfish Boxes to preview the weekend ahead. […]
fullText:
Although lacking the drama of their historical post season battles, the three game series forthcoming on Chicago’s south side holds heightened significance should the Astros hope to remain relevant this baseball season.

Len Kasper calls games for the White Sox and he joins us exclusively at The Crawfish Boxes to preview the weekend ahead.

Q: How personally fulfilling has this season been for you after witnessing the rebuild?

A: Super, super fun for Darrin Jackson and me. I recall a few weeks ago when the Sox were like 31-28 and we had the note that 2 years ago they were 31-109 I had to do a double take. I called all of those games and lived it but it still doesn’t seem real. Having said that, this season has really put all those struggles in the rear view mirror. It doesn’t matter anymore. This team is good and the way they play is FUN and we are living in the moment. They play hard, they slug, they claw from behind, they enjoy each other. There is something really special about this group that is hard to quantify, but when you see it, you acknowledge that it matters. Also, our fans adore this team. They love the winning but they love how this team plays just as much.

Q: How huge has a guy like Sean Newcomb been?

A: I think it’s fair to say he’s been the most valuable pitcher on the roster. He has done a little bit of everything which is where the league is now headed — closers, set-up men, etc. are becoming a thing of the past. Pitchers are just out-getters and in Newcomb’s case, you feel comfortable using him in any situation. What a great under-the-radar addition he’s been. One underrated thing about the bullpen is most of the guys are multi-inning options: Newcomb, Taylor, Hudson, Murphy, Richards, et al.

Q: Not to put it on one guy, but if Sean Burke continues the strong outings, you must feel pretty upbeat about the remaining two months of the season, correct?

A: Burke has pitched like an ace over the last several weeks. The stuff has always been there but it has been about strike-throwing and he is now doing that. One walk in his last 3 starts and a ton of strikeouts. I kinda hate the “this guy is a 1, this guy is a 3” conversation, BUT if we are gonna do that, the Sox have been looking for a “1” and right now, it’s Sean Burke. It’s interesting, they opened for him a few times earlier this season and he always pitched really well in that bulk relief role. But I’m guessing he didn’t love it and the best way to not be in that position is to pitch like he has. I wouldn’t expect an opener to be in play for him again for awhile.

Q: Biggest need at the deadline? Will it be another arm or a combination of things best guess?

A: These are questions for Chris Getz, but I just think the “you can never have enough pitching” cliche applies. I trust he will do everything he can to supplement the current roster while not sacrificing the future.

Q: I’m guessing if things stay the course, there will be some awards handed out on the south side for this unexpected season?

A: If the Sox make the playoffs, they will undoubtedly have the AL Manager of the Year and probably the Executive of the Year. Both would be well deserved. Will Venable has created a great culture here by allowing this group to kind of dictate the vibe. So many managers, even some of the all time greats, loom over all of it and sometimes that can dampen whatever the natural atmosphere might be. And while Will has some things he expects out of his guys and is very clear about those things, he has “stayed out of the way” to a degree in this area and that’s a huge thing here. As a former player, he understands how important it is for the nucleus to set the tone on a daily basis and it has made a very talented team even better. And Getz made a trade for Tristan Peters who came out of nowhere to become an All-Star, and another piece from the Crochet deal, Braden Montgomery, is now the everyday right fielder. Miguel Vargas has had a breakout season. The Murakami signing is looking like one of the best from last winter in the entire league. He has flipped this roster upside down and it’s now super young and on the position player side, one of the best in the entire league.

title: Rising Falcons star earns top-10 ranking at his position from PFF
description: Where does PFF rank Falcons TE Kyle Pitts ahead of 2026 season?
fullText:
Heading into the 2026 NFL Draft, there was a lot of trade speculation and chatter regarding the Atlanta Falcons and their former top-five overall pick, tight end Kyle Pitts.

In the end the Falcons either didn't get an offer they liked or decided that they'd rather keep Pitts and bank on his 2025 breakthrough as a positive trend and not an aberration.

So, Matt Ryan and the rest of Atlanta's new-look front office re-signed Pitts to a big contract, totaling $54 million over three years.

With the 2026 season just a handful of weeks away, Pitts is earning more accolades. Pro Football Focus has a new list of rankings out for the top 32 tight ends in the NFL. Pitts made the cut, coming in at No. 8 on their list, one spot ahead of aging Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce.

"After a relatively disappointing three-year stretch from 2022-2024, Pitts bounced back in a major way this past season. His 928 receiving yards were second in the NFL to only Trey McBride, as were his 88 receptions. Pitts tallied 51 receptions that went for either a first down or touchdown, the second-most in the league."

Eighth might seem a bit low for a tight end who ranks third in annual salary at his position, but this is a pretty fair ranking considering the relatively small sample size of the elite play we've seen from Pitts so far.

The seven tight ends around the league who PFF ranked ahead of him are George Kittle (49ers), Trey McBride (Cardinals), Brock Bowers (Raiders), Sam LaPorta (Lions), Colston Loveland (Bears), Dalton Kincaid (Bills) and Tucker Craft (Packers).

Looking ahead, Pitts should be moving up this list if he can stay healthy. In Kevin Stefanski's offense in Cleveland their top tight end David Njoku was a huge part of their offense until injuries slowed him down the last couple of years. Expect more of the same for Pitts - who has a far higher ceiling.

This article originally appeared on Falcons Wire: Rising Falcons star earns top-10 ranking at his position from PFF

title: Duke’s Official Roster Posted, With Some Surprises
description: According to GoDuke.com, Cayden Boozer has shed 5% of his body mass over the summer.
fullText:
As we’ve been starting our ACC basketball previews, we’ve looked periodically at GoDuke.com to see if they’ve posted the updated roster like most of the rest of the conference, and Thursday, they did.

First, Dame Sarr has muscled up a bit, as advertised: he’s now listed at 6-8 and 200 lbs., which is 10 more than last season, and it shows.

Not that this matters much, but Caleb Foster is down two pounds from his freshman weight. Minor, but interesting.

Cayden Boozer has apparently worked hard, and is down 10 pounds from last season, now weighing 195, which should help his quickness and endurance considerably.

We had seen Bryson Howard listed at 6-5, but Duke has him listed at 6-4.

John Blackwell was listed at 6-4 at Wisconsin, but Duke has him at 6-5.

This is not a huge surprise, but Maxime Meyer outweighs Cameron Williams. Meyer, who is 7-1, is now listed at 225, up about 10 pounds from his high school weight. Williams, who is listed at 7-0, is now 215. That’s notable because Meyer appears to have added 10 pounds pretty quickly, and Williams is an inch taller than previously listed.

Drew Scharnowski was listed at 6-9 and 230 last year at Belmont; this year, Duke has him at 6-10 and 240.

Lastly, and most surprisingly, Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje is listed at 7-2 and 250, which is exactly what Khaman Maluach was listed at when he was at Duke.

Boumtje Boumtje was listed at 6-10 this summer with Team USA for the U17 FIBA, and while it might possible that he grew three inches since early July, call us skeptical.

Well, there could be a number of reasons. Some measurements may have been done with shoes on or off, for one. For Boumtje Boumtje, it’s possible that someone screwed up the conversion from metric to the U.S. customary system.

Some guys may have been rounded up as well. Williams could easily have grown a half-inch over the summer, and they might have just rounded him up to 7-0.

If they are bumping up heights systematically, someone dropped the ball on Howard, who apparently shrank.

However you look at it, this will again be a very tall team: the average height is 6-7, and that’s going to be one of the bigger teams in the country.

Two of those players, Chambliss and Carr, were relative unknowns at this point last year. title: Michigan's top-rated hoops prospect in 2027 to transfer out of state
description: For the third time in two years, a blue-chip basketball recruit will leave Michigan to play in an academy.
fullText:
For the third time in two years, a blue-chip high school basketball recruit will leave Michigan to play elsewhere.

Christian Cast, a star guard at Detroit Country Day and favorite to win Michigan Mr. Basketball next season, will leave southeast Michigan and transfer to Monarch Academy (formerly Link Academy), his father, Adolphus Cast, tells the Detroit Free Press.

Cast, a 6-foot-3 and 175-pound combo guard, is a three-star recruit, the No. 1 player in Michigan, No. 24 combo guard in the country and No. 161 player in the class of 2027, according to 247Sports composite rankings.

Cast has prep schools across the country offering six figures for his services, per his father, but has decided to transfer to the newly-formed elite Nike EYBL Scholastic prep basketball program located in Kansas City.

"We're choosing to take the harder route, go to this school with all these five stars and train," Adolphus Cast said. "So we want to take advantage and get ready for his professional career, which is college now, which is crazy."

Adolphus Cast said this wasn't a decision the family made lightly, saying they still "love Country Day" and "there's no bad energy with us and the coach."

Even when Michigan basketball legend Chris Webber called to try and convince the standout to stay at his alma mater, they felt leaving was the right decision.

First, Cast only needs four credits to graduate, but Detroit Country Day could not amend its rules, which requires students to take six or seven classes. Recently, Cast has been waking up at 6 a.m. to workout, goes to school, then does one or two practices or training sessions after class, which was untenable.

ON THE GRIDIRON: Top 10 running backs to watch in 2026 Michigan high school football

At Monarch, which according to the school website, aims to "deliver a blended academic program designed around the student-athlete schedule," Cast will be able to take four classes and have more free time to prepare athletically.

"We love Michigan, but we have to take you know the next step to be ready," Adolphus Cast said. "The last kid that was ranked No. 1, Carlos Medlock (now at Michigan State), last year had to kind of do the same thing."

Equally as importantly is the level of play. The Cast family believes there is a "level of competition" and a "certain nutrition and lifting regimen" that is required to reach the highest level.

Cast played this summer on the Power 5 3SSB (Adidas) circuit where he was named first-team in two of three sessions and second-team on the other.

Last season for Detroit Country Day he was named first-team All-State in Class B by the Detroit Free Press. At the time of his nomination, he was averaging 24 points, six assists, six rebounds and two steals per night as he shot 41% on 3s and 87% on free throws.

Cast currently holds Power Four offers from Arizona, Penn State and Mississippi State, per his father, and has been highly sought after by some mid-majors. That includes one in the MAC that Adolphus Cast says has offered a multi-year NIL deal that's above seven figures − the program told the family it's the largest they've ever offered for an incoming freshman.

Michigan and Michigan State are both interested, too. MSU has reached out to him to attend "grind week," which is an annual tradition in the program, typically in early September, when former players return to East Lansing for workouts, mentoring and bonding with current and prospective players.

Michigan has been in contact with Cast nearly every day but also has not extended an official offer.

Both would be among Cast's top options along with Arkansas and Oklahoma, but he will no longer be just a short drive away for either Tom Izzo or Mike Boynton Jr. this season. It's not what the family wanted, but the business of the sport continues to start earlier and earlier.

Once again − like it was with Medlock and Mateen Cleaves Jr. − it's the MHSAA's loss.

"It's kind of disappointing that we [feel we] have to leave as a parent," Adolphus Cast said. "It's an unfortunate thing, but it has to happen if you're really trying to play at that level."

Tony Garcia is the Wolverines beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia.

title: Sabrina Ionescu 'didn't get invited' to defend WNBA 3-point crown
description: New York Liberty guard Sabrina Ionescu said she did not receive an official invitation to participate in this year’s WNBA three-point contest.
fullText:
New York Liberty star guard Sabrina Ionescu clarified on July 22 that she never officially received an invitation to defend her title in this year’s WNBA 3-point Contest and was surprised by reports that it was her choice not to participate.

In a press conference ahead of WNBA All-Star weekend, Ionescu said she was blindsided by media headlines suggesting she had declined an offer to participate. She emphasized her eagerness to compete whenever given the opportunity, but reiterated that she could not turn down an invitation she never received.

“I can’t decline an offer that I officially didn’t get invited to,” Ionescu said. “So I was pretty surprised to see that. Never got invited. Whether it's against Steph Curry or in the W, I always go out and try to beat my record every single time I step onto the court. I take pride in competing at the highest level, and I love representing the Liberty and the league in these contests. I just wanted to set the record straight – that rumor was simply false.”

"I can't decline an offer I never officially got invited to."

Sabrina Ionescu would've loved to beat her record in the three point contest, but the invite from the WNBA never came. pic.twitter.com/YRijofzzGR

— Sportico (@Sportico) July 22, 2026

Though she isn’t taking part in this year’s contest, Ionescu said she was excited to watch the event and to see who will become the new champion.

To Ionescu’s claim that she never received an invite, the WNBA responded with a statement saying, “Our general process is to reach out to agents to determine a player's interest, and some accept and some decline."

Ionescu is just the second player in league history to win multiple titles, winning in 2023 and 2025.

In 2025, she secured the title by scoring 30 of 40 points in the final round, surpassing Allisha Gray, who scored 22. Ionescu’s 30-point performance in 2025 came close to the league record of 37 points, which she set in 2023.

title: Biggest NBA offseason overreaction isn’t justified
description: NBA fan and media are overreacting far too much about this trade
fullText:
As NBA free agency dies down and the Summer League comes to an end, there’s less going on in the basketball world. Which means there’s going to be a lot more opinions and predictions. There have been countless blockbuster trades and signings this offseason, leaving people with plenty to talk about.

Undoubtedly, the biggest move of the offseason was Boston sending former Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia in exchange for Paul George and a couple of second-round picks. The majority of analysts and talking heads have already written the Celtics off, but is it a bit premature?

MORE: 3 NBA teams who are most improved entering 2026-2027 season

People are acting like Boston moving on from Jaylen Brown is the end-all, be-all. Boston did downgrade at the shooting guard position, slotting an aging Paul George into his place, but they also improved in other areas.

Their most significant upgrade came at center. It’s no secret that Boston has been searching for a reliable, physical center. They have brought in several players, but none could meet their expectations. They finally signed Knicks center Mitchell Robinson this offseason in hopes that he can solve that issue.

Robinson is an improvement over Nikola Vučević, and only time will tell how big of an impact this move will make.

Jaylen Brown is not a player you can easily replace, but how big of a downgrade is Paul George?

George is an above-average defender and a reliable scorer. He doesn’t measure up to Jaylen Brown, but in no way is he a bad basketball player. George averaged 17 points per game while shooting 40 percent from beyond the arc.

George provides a similar playstyle to Jaylen Brown while being less ball-dominant and a bit worse in nearly every area.

MORE: 3 NBA teams that have quietly won the offseason already

Boston made this trade to make it clear that Jayson Tatum is their guy. They essentially handed the keys to the offense to him, displaying full trust in their young superstar.

They improved at center and removed a ball-dominant player. The Celtics were able to finish second in the East without Tatum and with a lackluster center. With Tatum and a better center, who’s to say this team can’t finish first?

title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty shrugs off bizarre delay to emerge fastest in Commonwealth breaststroke heats
description: Ramsay-Peaty’s 100m heat was temporarily halted as he was on the blocks when a lane divider broke off
fullText:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty shrugged off a bizarre delay to power through to the semi-finals of the men’s 100 metres breaststroke event at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Ramsay-Peaty’s heat was temporarily halted as he was on the blocks when a lane divider broke off, requiring an official to strip to the waist and enter the pool to reconnect it.

Ramsay-Peaty duly wasted no time in recording the fastest time of the morning, 59.46 seconds, with only two rivals, Australia’s Sam Williamson and Filip Nowacki of Jersey, also finishing in under a minute.

The three-time Olympic champion is taking part in his fourth Commonwealth Games having clinched his first medals as a 19-year-old in Glasgow in 2014.

Since then he has become a fixture of the gossip columns after marrying Holly Ramsay, daughter of celebrity chef Gordon, in December last year, and experiencing a rift with the majority of his family.

Ramsay-Peaty has described these Games as a “full circle moment” as he looks to reignite his career. A silver medal at the Paris Olympics in 2024 helped him refocus after a difficult 2023 in which he withdrew from a series of events in order to focus on mental health concerns.

His win in the 100m in 2014 began eight years of almost total dominance in the event. That streak came to an end in dramatic fashion in Birmingham four years ago when he trailed home in a shock fourth place in the event.

Ramsay-Peaty, who is due to return for his semi-final on Friday evening, told TNT Sports: “Job done, really. We’ve got a busy two weeks coming up, so we’re reserving energy where we can.

“Last time I was here, I was very young. We barely had any world records to my name, or known world records to my name, so it’s been a very long journey.”

title: SPL announces 2026-27 RSL fixture schedule
description: The Saudi Pro League (SPL) has confirmed the fixture schedule for the 2026-27 Roshn Saudi League season, with the campaign set to begin on August 13, 2026, and conclude on May 29, 2027.The 34-round se...
fullText:
The Saudi Pro League (SPL) has confirmed the fixture schedule for the 2026-27 Roshn Saudi League season, with the campaign set to begin on August 13, 2026, and conclude on May 29, 2027.

The 34-round season will feature 306 matches, with the fixture list finalised on Friday following a workshop attended by all clubs. During the session, the SPL presented the scheduling methodology and the wider sporting calendar, while clubs were also invited to submit requests regarding match sequencing and scheduling before the fixtures were approved.

The 2026-27 calendar has been developed against the backdrop of an exceptionally demanding season, with eight RSL clubs competing across four international competitions, alongside FIFA international windows, Saudi Arabia national team commitments and the Kingdom's hosting of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup.

As a result of these overlapping commitments, only 102 available matchdays were available to accommodate the league's 306 fixtures.

To ensure a balanced and competitive schedule, the fixture list was created using 10 key scheduling criteria. Among the most significant are that no club will play more than two consecutive home or away matches, while every club will play one home and one away fixture across the opening and closing two rounds of the 2026-27 campaign.

In addition, all clubs are guaranteed a minimum rest period of two days between consecutive matches, regardless of the competition in which they are participating.

As part of the scheduling process, clubs were divided into four competitive tiers to help distribute fixtures evenly and avoid prolonged sequences against the strongest opposition. Under this model, no club will face a "Level A" opponent in consecutive league rounds.

The classifications are as follows:

Level A: Al Nassr, Al Hilal, Al Ahli, Al Qadsiah and Al Ittihad

Level B: Al Taawoun, Al Ettifaq, Al Fateh, Al Khaleej and Al Shabab

Level C:  NEOM Sports Club, Al Hazem, Al Fayha and Al Kholood,

Level D: Al Riyadh, Abha, Al Faisaly and Diriyah FC

The rankings were determined using a sporting performance model based on results from the previous three seasons, with greater weighting given to the most recent campaign to provide a balanced and objective basis for the scheduling process.

Operational considerations also played a key role, including stadium availability and venue requirements arising from the Kingdom's hosting of regional, continental and international events.

The SPL confirmed that the fixture schedule has been designed to strike the best possible balance between sporting integrity, competitive fairness, club participation across multiple competitions, stadium operations and the overall fan experience.

title: Indiana football player, Warren Central grad arrested on strangulation, domestic battery charges
description: Tyrone Burrus Jr. was arrested in Bloomington on Thursday. Here's what we know as this story develops.
fullText:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana football defensive end Tyrone Burrus Jr. was arrested by the Bloomington Police Department on Thursday.

According to an officer at the Monroe County jail, Burrus was booked on preliminary charges of strangulation and domestic battery. The strangulation charge is a Level 6 felony, while the domestic battery charge is a Class A misdemeanor. In Indiana, a Level 6 felony conviction carries a penalty of six months to two-and-a-half years in prison with fines up to $10,000.

Burrus remained in custody at the jail as of Friday morning, per a jail officer. According to a clerk at the Monroe Circuit Court, Burrus' initial court appearance hasn't been scheduled, but the earliest it could happen is on Monday.

“IU Athletics is aware of the situation,” an IU spokesperson told The Herald-Times, part of the USA TODAY Network. “We will continue to gather facts, cooperate with and monitor the legal process, and take further action as the evolving situation warrants.”

Burrus, a Warren Central grad out of Indianapolis, played in two games last season while redshirting. He made his college debut in IU’s 56-3 win over Purdue and made his first career tackle. He had a more prominent role in the Peach Bowl against Oregon with injuries piling up for the Hoosiers at defensive end.

Going into 2026, Burrus was part of a large group of young defensive lineman looking to crack into Indiana’s rotation. He came through with a sack in IU’s spring game.

Burrus originally committed to Louisville, but ended up signing with the Hoosiers in 2025 as the No. 9-ranked player in the state.

title: Salvador Perez makes heartfelt plea after fan arrested retrieving historic home run
description: A Royals fan jumped into the Kauffman Stadium fountains to recover Salvador Perez’s record-tying home run ball, leading to an arrest and a personal request from the Kansas City captain.  Salvador Perez understood why one Kansas City Royals fan was willing to risk a trip to jail for a piece of franchise history.  Perez blasted the 317th home run of his career Wednesday against the San Francisco Giants, tying Hall of Famer George Brett for the most in Royals history.
fullText:
Salvador Perez makes heartfelt plea after fan arrested retrieving historic home run originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

A Royals fan jumped into the Kauffman Stadium fountains to recover Salvador Perez’s record-tying home run ball, leading to an arrest and a personal request from the Kansas City captain.

Salvador Perez understood why one Kansas City Royals fan was willing to risk a trip to jail for a piece of franchise history.

Perez blasted the 317th home run of his career Wednesday against the San Francisco Giants, tying Hall of Famer George Brett for the most in Royals history. The 437-foot drive landed in the famous fountains beyond the right-center-field wall at Kauffman Stadium.

One fan decided that history was worth getting wet for. The fan jumped into the fountain in an attempt to retrieve Perez’s home run ball. Security quickly intervened, escorting the fan out of the stadium before police placed him in handcuffs and took him into custody.

When Perez learned what happened, the longtime Royals catcher made a public plea for authorities to show the fan some mercy.

“Please, police, just take him out of the jail, please,” Perez said, according to a video shared by Jomboy Media.

Perez acknowledged that he might have made the same decision if he had been in the fan’s position.

“If I was him, I’d maybe jump too and try to get that ball,” Perez said. “So please, and thank you for the hard work in trying to get that ball.”

The fan was later released, according to FOX4 Kansas City.

Kauffman Stadium is known for the fountains that stretch across the outfield, but fans are strictly prohibited from entering the water. The Royals’ guest rules state that anyone entering a fountain will be immediately arrested, taken to a downtown police station and charged. That policy did not stop the fan from pursuing one of the most significant home run balls in franchise history.

"Please police just take him out of the jail please." -Salvador Perez after a fan was arrested for jumping in the fountain to retrieve his home run ball that tied the Royals franchise record pic.twitter.com/dPxpUVhyb4

— Jomboy Media (@JomboyMedia) July 23, 2026

The unusual scene added another memorable chapter to an already unforgettable afternoon for Perez and the Royals. Kansas City trailed San Francisco when Perez stepped to the plate in the seventh inning. His two-run homer cut the Giants’ lead and sparked a four-run rally. Lane Thomas later delivered a go-ahead two-run single, lifting the Royals to a 5-4 victory.

Perez finished the day tied with Brett at the top of the franchise leaderboard. Mike Sweeney ranks a distant third with 197 home runs, followed by Amos Otis at 193 and Alex Gordon at 190.

MORE: Red Sox winning streak ends at 15, but historic run changes everything in Boston

Perez has spent his entire 15-year MLB career with Kansas City, developing into one of the most decorated and beloved players in club history. The 36-year-old is a nine-time All-Star, five-time Gold Glove winner and five-time Silver Slugger. He was also named World Series MVP after helping the Royals defeat the New York Mets in 2015.

Royals manager Matt Quatraro became emotional while discussing what Perez has meant to the organization.

“I love that guy,” Quatraro said. “What he does, the way he goes about it, the passion he plays the game with, it’s unrivaled. The guy’s a Hall of Famer, and you’re getting to witness it.”

Perez was grateful that his record-tying homer came in front of the home crowd.

“That was a super exciting moment,” Perez said. “Especially doing it here in Kansas City. I love the fans here. Kansas City is my second home.”

One fan apparently loved the moment enough to take an unexpected swim and spend part of the celebration in police custody. Fortunately for him, he had the Royals captain firmly on his side.

title: 10 Hacks Every AirTag User Should Know
description: If you use AirTags to track your things, these hacks will make them even more useful.
fullText:
AirTags can be exceptionally useful trackers. These tiny devices passively beam their locations to any passing iPhone, iPad, or Find My-enabled device, which makes it possible to track items like keys and bags when they go missing. They're not difficult to set up and use: Once they're in place, they're good to go—until their batteries die about a year later.

But while AirTags are simple, there's a lot you can do with them. You can locate missing tags in futuristic ways; use them as NFC tags to run automations with a scan of your iPhone; and you can share their locations with airlines to help locate your luggage when it goes missing. Whether you own one AirTag or many, you need to know about these 10 hacks to make the most of your trackers.

AirTags are meant to find things you've lost, but there are many ways to find them. You can use Precision Finding on your iPhone to see guided directions to your missing AirTag, assuming it's within Bluetooth range. However, if you have the right kind of Apple Watch and the right kind of AirTag, you can use your watch to track down your tracker via Precision Finding, too.

To use Precision Finding, you need an Apple Watch Series 9 or newer, or an Ultra 2 or newer, as well as a second-generation AirTag. To set it up, open Control Center on your watch, then scroll to the bottom and choose "Edit." Here, tap (+), choose "Find Items," then choose "Find AirTag." Tap Choose, then tap an item from your existing AirTags. Tap "Done." Now, you're set to find that item in the future. When you need to, return to Control Center, then tap the "Find AirTag" button. If the AirTag is somewhere within range, you'll see guided directions on your Apple Watch.

Depending on your situation, your fastest location method might be via Siri. If you're sure the AirTag you're missing is nearby, just pull out your iPhone (or your Apple Watch) and ask Siri where your item is. (e.g. "Hey Siri, where is my backpack?" or "Where are my keys?" Siri will "think" for a moment, and, if it can find them, will start pinging your AirTag, so you can follow the sound to locate them.

Apple's "Left Behind" alerts can be useful. If you leave your house without your keys, for example, you might appreciate that notification letting you know. But if you have an AirTag in something you don't take with you every day—perhaps a suitcase or a backpack—you don't need your iPhone buzzing every time you step out your door. Then again, should you leave your hotel room without your suitcase, you may want that heads up before hopping in the Uber to the airport.

As such, you should whitelist specific locations where your AirTags can stay behind without triggering one of these alerts. That way, you can keep the notifications on in general, but spare your sanity whenever leaving items behind in a known location. Your iPhone may even do this for you automatically, depending on the locations it thinks you don't need the alerts from. However, you can add or remove any locations manually to your liking.

To set this up, open Find My on your iPhone, tap "Items," then choose the AirTag you want to adjust settings for. Here, scroll down, then choose "Notify When Left Behind." If the feature isn't on, enable it, then look down to "Notify me, except at:" Here, you can remove any automatically added locations, or add new ones by hitting "New Location."

When your AirTags' batteries are low (or, let's face it, dead), you can replace them yourself—assuming you bought the proper batteries. But they're not the easiest to open up: You have to press down on the silver back of your AirTag and rotate it counterclockwise until the cover comes loose. If you're having trouble getting it to work, you're not alone. But there's a simple hack to make it a bit easier.

I stumbled upon this via MacGeekGab on YouTube. The idea is, take a small amount of tape on the back, then use that as a grip to help with the twist. MacGeekGab also recommends using rubber thimbles, like the kind you use to count money, to achieve the same effect. The next time your AirTag's battery bites the dust, give this trick a shot.

AirTags are great for luggage: You can pop one in your bag and track it down if it goes missing or gets left behind. That includes if your airline loses your bag. Not only can you show them the Find My app on your iPhone, but you can share your AirTag with your airline directly, so they can help pinpoint its location.

To do so, head to the "Items" tab in Find My, then tap the AirTag for the missing luggage. Under "Lost AirTag," tap "Share Item Location." (This will only work if the AirTag is not within range.) From here, you can follow the on-screen instructions to share the AirTag with your airline, and hope that they'll be able to find it on their end.

In a similar vein, you can share your AirTag with a contact. That way, not only can they keep tabs on the AirTag's location, they won't receive tracking notifications for the item. (In other words, their iPhone won't assume your AirTag is silently tracking them, and will not alert them as such.) To share an AirTag, open it in your Find My app, then, under "Share AirTag," choose "Add Person." Tap "Continue," then choose a contact or contacts to share your AirTag with. When finished, tap the check mark in the top right.

Your AirTag isn't just a tracker; it's also an NFC tag. This technology is what makes tap-to-pay work: You wave your iPhone over the tag, which triggers some pre-planned action. In this case, you can set up your AirTag to run any automation you want in Apple Shortcuts. For example, this Redditor uses it to remind themselves to take their medication; if they don't scan their AirTag, which they've stuck underneath the lid of their medication bottle, they'll receive a reminder.

To start setting up your AirTag as an NFC tag, open Shortcuts on your iPhone, then choose the "Automations" tab. Here, tap the (+) in the top right, then scroll down and choose "NFC." Tap "NFC Tag — Scan," then wave your iPhone over your AirTag. This can be a bit tricky, just as it can be difficult to get tap-to-pay to work. But I've found pointing the top of my iPhone at the AirTag to work best. Once it takes, name the tag whatever you want, then hit "OK." From here, the world is your oyster; you can choose any app or shortcut to run when you scan your AirTag.

As it happens, your AirTag has a default NFC function as-is: to pull up the contact info for an owner's AirTag after it goes missing. As such, you could be on both sides of this problem. If your AirTag goes missing, you should activate Lost Mode so that someone can scan it with their iPhone. But if you find one in the wild, you shouldn't just pick it up and ask if it belongs to anyone nearby. You can tap it with your iPhone like you would when paying at a POS, and, if it's in Lost Mode, you should see the owner's info.

To set this up on your end, open the AirTag in your Find My app, then, under Lost Mode, choose "Show Contact Info." Tap "Continue," then follow the on-screen prompts. (Again, this only works if your AirTag is not with you.)

If your AirTag isn't working properly, but its battery still has plenty of juice left in it, you can try a factory reset to get things working again. This will reset the AirTag to its original settings, which means it will unpair with your Apple Account. As such, not only is it an option if things aren't working as they should, but it's also an easy way to give your AirTag to someone else if you no longer want or need it.

To reset your AirTag, first identify whether it is a first-gen or second-gen AirTag. The instructions are slightly different depending on which you have. You can do so by identifying the serial number on the inside of your AirTag. Once you do, follow Apple's instructions here depending on your AirTag generation.

AirTags are designed to run for about a year before their batteries die. That's not a bad battery life for a piece of tech. However, not all AirTags are used the same. While the AirTag on your keys is used all the time, the one in your suitcase might not be. If you only take your luggage out every few months or so, your AirTag is slowly burning through a battery it doesn't actually need to be using.

Unfortunately, you can't put an AirTag into standby mode, or enable something like a Low Power Mode. Instead, consider removing the battery for any AirTags that aren't frequent fliers. That's what YouTuber HotshotTek does with his, and, in fact, tapes the battery to the front of their AirTag to keep it ready to go when they need it.

title: McClenaghan set to qualify for pommel horse final
description: Olympic champion Rhys McClenaghan all but secures his passage to the Commonwealth Games pommel horse final as he posts a score of 14.500 after a flawless display with his new routine.
fullText:
Olympic champion Rhys McClenaghan all but secured his passage to the Commonwealth Games pommel horse final as he posted the highest score of 14.500 after a flawless display with his new routine.

All eyes in the Emirates Arena were on McClenaghan and he delivered, even celebrating with a jig after stepping off the apparatus.

The 27-year-old tops the qualifying standings after two subdivisions which all but ensures he will be in Monday's final.

Confirmation of his place in the final will come after the third subdivision of qualifying, which takes place at 17:30 BST, but McClenaghan is already well clear of those closest to him.

McClenaghan, who missed the entirety of 2025 after shoulder surgery, earned an difficult score of 5.500 and an execution score of 9.000, both the highest so far in qualifying.

He is aiming to win his third Commonwealth Games medal after picking up gold in 2018 and silver in 2022.

Ewan McAteer moved into second in vault qualifying as he finished with a score of 13.650.

title: Devlin opens up on 'too stressful' Hearts exit for Rangers
description: Cammy Devlin says it was "too stressful" to head to the World Cup with his club future still to be decided - although the extra time taken did lead to a move to Rangers.
fullText:
Cammy Devlin says it was "too stressful" to head to the World Cup with his club future still to be decided, although the extra time taken did lead to a move to Rangers "that was too good to pass up".

The 28-year-old midfielder's contract was running down as he joined the Australia squad just three days after being "devastated" by the final-day loss to Celtic that meant Heart of Midlothian were pipped to the Scottish title by their hosts.

Devlin was weighing up whether to accept a new deal from the Edinburgh club amid rival interest, before Derek McInnes' own switch from Hearts to become Rangers manager decided the midfielder's destiny.

"The game was on the Saturday and I flew out to the World Cup on the Tuesday," Devlin said in his first public interview since joining the Glasgow club.

Rangers buy Serbia's Dragojevic from Partizan

Pandur joined Rangers after Hull planned new number one

Devlin sees McInnes relationship bloom already for Rangers

"It was devastating, but I didn't have much time to reflect on how last season ended and then straight into the World Cup, which is one of the most special moments of your career.

"My mum, my dad and my girlfriend are over in America supporting you. So you are trying to enjoy that as much as you can.

"I thought it would be a good idea going there off-contract, but it wasn't.

"It was too stressful. It was hard just being in the moment being at the World Cup and dealing with all that and the noise around it, and my dad asking me every day what's going on."

Devlin failed to add to his five Australia caps at the World Cup and a week after their last-32 defeat by Egypt, Hearts announced he would not be signing a new contract, with Rangers announcing his capture the following day.

McInnes had gone from a position of trying to persuade Devlin to stay at Tynecastle one week to one of enticing the midfielder to Ibrox the next.

"Everyone knows the relationship I have with the gaffer where we are super close and he was so good for me at Hearts and everyone knows the season we had there," Devlin said. "He helped me so much as a player.

"I was not trying to focus on it too much and just enjoy the World Cup, but when the opportunity came, it was one that was too good to pass up."

Devlin says it was "a hard decision to make" to leave Hearts.

"Hearts is such a special football club and I will be forever grateful for giving me the opportunity to play football outside Australia," he said.

"There were obviously other things I had to weigh up with Hearts - I've never been in that position where I've been off-contract.

"Rangers was one that came a bit later and I've been in Scotland for quite a while now and know how big a football club it is.

"Being a Rangers player is super special and something I never thought would happen. It was just something I couldn't say no to."

As for last season's title heartache, Devlin added: "Football is cruel sometimes and you just have to pick yourself up and take the next opportunity.

"Hopefully I can go one better with Rangers."

title: Meet the Glasgow curry shop boss representing Pakistan at bowls
description: Mohammed 'Chico' Qureshi has called Glasgow home for more than 50 years, but he will represent Pakistan against Scotland at the Commonwealth Games on Friday.
fullText:
Scottish bowler Jason Banks is fond of the Alishan Tandoori in Glasgow. But he knows it is best to avoid it this week.

Why? Because Pakistan's Mohammed 'Chico' Qureshi - who Banks will face in the Commonwealth Games men's singles on Friday - runs the restaurant.

While Banks was the first Team Scotland athlete to compete at these Games - as he defeated Robert Simpson of Jamaica in straight sets - you would be forgiven for thinking otherwise, as the well-supported Qureshi took to the portable rink at the SEC Centre in the session prior.

Pakistan was the name on the back of his shirt, but the 67-year-old restaurateur - who competed at the 2014 Games - has called Glasgow home for over 50 years.

Is 2026 the Commonwealth Games' last dance or a future-proofing revamp?

Five big names to look out for at Glasgow 2026

It was something of a dream for Qureshi to go again in a second home Games after taking to the outdoor green at Kelvingrove 12 years ago.

A member at Glasgow Indoor Bowling Club - just round the corner from his restaurant - he had been putting in the hours to be ready for the conditions awaiting him in his opening match against Wales' Ross Owen.

Unfortunately, it did not quite go to plan as he lost in straight sets - 12-5 and 17-0.

"That's the worst game I've ever played," a still upbeat Qureshi told BBC Scotland. "It was very tricky to get going. The more I was trying, the worse I was getting."

All is far from lost, though, with four Group C games still to go.

On the carpet, Qureshi is hoping for much improvement. Off it, he is not sure if he has scared his supporters away.

"I had a few here," he said. "But, with my performance, I don't think they'll come back again!"

As long as they keep coming back to the restaurant, though. Because, for now, they have lost the custom of Banks.

The former world number one - who held the world indoor singles, pairs and mixed pairs titles last year - has been known to dine in Glasgow's southside, but he is heading elsewhere for now.

"I'm a bit scared to go back this week in case he puts something in my food," the 30-year-old from Inverurie joked. "So I'll stay away just now."

Banks faces Qureshi at 16:45 on Friday.

title: Boxers choose Commonwealths over Love Island chance
description: Team Northern Ireland boxers Jon McConnell and Kaci Rock talk about choosing the Commonwealth Games over potentially appearing on Love Island.
fullText:
It could have been a very different summer for two members of Northern Ireland's 12-strong boxing team.

Jon McConnell and Kaci Rock will compete in this year's Commonwealth Games for the first time, but had progressed through the initial auditions for the latest series of Love Island before pulling out because the TV show clashes in timing with the Games.

McConnell, who competed at the recent World Boxing Cup in Brazil, will compete in the light-middleweight division and will face India's Sumit Sumit on Monday, with Holy Trinity's Rock in welterweight action against Niue's Karen Te Ruki Pasene the following day.

Reality TV show Love Island, hosted by Maya Jama, has just completed its 13th series in Mallorca.

"I used to spend a lot of time watching Love Island with the team," said 23-year-old McConnell.

"It was never really my idea at first, but Kaci mentioned it and said she'd put my name forward as well.

"I got through a few stages of the process but then I got selected for the Commonwealth Games."

Rock is aiming to follow in the footsteps of her dad, Jim Rock, the only boxer to have won Irish titles across four weights.

The 23-year-old is one of five boxers in the team that are one win away from a Commonwealth Games' medal.

"Me and Jon have been friends for years and I joked about going on it one day," Rock said.

"The two of us got to the same point but then we said, 'Oh God, it's too soon'. I'd rather make my name in sport than anything else."

Rock does not intend to audition for the TV show again next year, but McConnell did not rule out making an appearance.

"If they want to give me a call after I've won a gold medal, they're welcome," said McConnell.

"Maybe I'll be standing on the podium with my medal around my neck and they can reach out to me then."

title: Scotland's Gunn concedes four in San Jose debut defeat
description: Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn suffers a nightmare debut for San Jose Earthquakes as they slump to a 4-0 defeat at home to Orlando City in their first match following Major League Soccer's break for the World Cup.
fullText:
Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn suffered a nightmare debut for San Jose Earthquakes as they slumped to a 4-0 defeat at home to Orlando City in their first match following Major League Soccer's break for the World Cup.

It was the 30-year-old's first game since his national side failed to qualify for the knockout stages following a 3-0 loss to Brazil in their final group game - and his first club game since coming on as a substitute in Nottingham Forest's 1-1 Premier League draw with Crystal Palace in February.

But, in truth, Gunn could take little blame for any of the goals while also producing a couple of saves that prevented a more painful loss for Bruce Arena's hosts.

Who has your Premiership club brought in & let go this summer?

Socceroos star allegedly tests positive for cocaine after speeding

Italy confirm Ancelotti approach before Guardiola

Visiting centre-half David Brekalo was left unmarked as he headed home Eduard Atuesta's free-kick with just seven minutes gone.

Winger Ivan Angulo doubled City's lead in the 29th minute with a powerful low drive into the far corner from just outside the penalty box.

France legend Antoine Griezmann marked his debut following the 35-year-old forward's move from Atletico Madrid by firing home from just inside the box three minutes after the break as Gunn was left exposed by a loss of possession.

Paraguay midfielder Braian Ojeda completed the rout in the 73rd minute as his header squeezed between Gunn and the near post from another Atuesta set piece.

At the other end, Gunn's opposite number, Canada's Maxime Crepeau, produced several fine saves, a couple denying Timo Werner a scoring debut for San Jose after the Germany striker's move from RB Leipzig.

Despite the defeat, Gunn's side remain tied on points at the top of the Western Conference but second on goal difference behind Vancouver Whitecaps, who lost 4-3 away to Cincinnati but have a game in hand.

San Jose are fourth in the overall table, with Nashville leading ahead of Argentina forward Lionel Messi's Inter Miami.

Gunn's side next host LA Galaxy, who are ninth in the Eastern Conference, on Sunday.

title: Why is it so special to be part of Team Scotland?
description: Competing for Scotland is a rare opportunity. BBC Scotland takes a look at why it means so much.
fullText:
There's the girl you know from your home town. The boy you went to university with. The fella who trains in the same gym as you every day. And your best pal and training partner is there, too.

None of you are having to speak slowly, to clip your Rs, or accentuate your vowels. You understand the patter, know what square sausage is, and can fluently punctuate by swearing.

It's like being among family and friends, with all the tender aggression and familiar hinterland that brings.

That is the atmosphere within Team Scotland, a diverse - yet similar - collection of athletes and staff who represent the country once every four years at the Commonwealth Games and will do so again in Glasgow in 2026.

"There's just something about being Scottish - we all just get it and that identity really resonates with us," says swimmer and Olympic and Commonwealth Games veteran Ross Murdoch.

"It's a completely different dynamic to Team GB. Everyone's just… it's a breath of fresh air," adds Olympic silver and bronze-winning cyclist Jack Carlin.

"It's warmer and more intimate," says Commonwealth badminton medallist Kirsty Gilmour. "With GB, you need to put your extrovert mask on and try to make new friends, but you just feel more at ease in Team Scotland."

Scotland agrees to host Commonwealth Games in 2026

What do athletes think about Glasgow 2026?

Those three athletes have also competed regularly for Britain and are at pains to make it clear that they enjoy, and even relish, doing so. But the Commonwealths are a rare chance to represent Scotland. Their country. Where they are from.

For most, the divergence is not political either. Instead, it is something far less tangible. A feeling. That's why explaining it isn't easy, particular for people whose sporting talents are their primary means of expression.

Ask athletes why it is special to represent Scotland and most immediately reach for the rarity of the opportunity.

In some sports, it only happens once every four years.

But there must be more to it than that? Not least because the Commonwealths lacks a little of the cachet of other events.

"Something just feels different when you're running for Scotland," says distance runner Eilish McColgan, who won a stunning gold medal in the Women's 10,000m in Birmingham in 2022.

"It's like I'm representing my home town - Dundee - a little bit more.

"You're around people you've known since you were wee - the athletes you've grown up with, the coaches, the support staff. And, when you were young, it wasn't about running for GB. It was about running for Scotland. So it just reminds you of home."

The feeling is rooted in childhood for Murdoch, too.

"Just putting on the Scotland kit brings me back to being a wee boy," he says. "I'm from a wee estate in the Vale of Leven and I remember watching Scotland winning medals at the 2006 Commonwealths and that seemed as big as the world could get.

"From then on, that was all I wanted to do, so for this hobby of mine to get totally out of hand and me do this three times… I can't even put that into words."

Hammer thrower Mark Dry has - like Murdoch, Carlin, McColgan and Gilmour - been to Olympics and world championships and is "proud" to have represented Britain. But none of those occasions, while materially more illustrious, have made him feel "anything like competing for Scotland does".

"It means everything to me," he says. "Other championships, you're doing it for yourself, but at the Commonwealths, you're doing it for Scotland."

Boxer Reese Lynch, who made his Games debut in Birmingham, is of a similar mind. "Even when I'm competing for GB, I'm still representing Scotland," he says. "It's where I'm from and it's who I am."

The identity is one aspect of it then. But the environment plays a part, too.

Being inside the Team GB machine at an Olympics can be a stifling, lonely and isolated experience. It is a very serious business, where everyone has "their game-face on", according to Gilmour.

Given these are athletes at the very pinnacle of their sport, that is perhaps how it should be. But it is also telling how many athletes will mention the atmosphere inside the Team Scotland camp as being something they crave every four years.

"For me, it's really good fun," says swimmer Duncan Scott, Scotland's most decorated Games athlete.

That's not to say that the business of winning medals is taken lightly, though. "It's more of a fun rivalry," says veteran Para-cyclist Neil Fachie.

"You've got your British team-mates there, and the Australians seem to get up for it a bit more, but the stress level is slightly lower, and the fun's a bit higher."

"There's no pressure," adds wheelchair racer Sammi Kinghorn. "There is such a spread of athletes and abilities and we are all so grateful to be there. If you win a medal, you come back to the village and everyone is so excited for you."

"It's what I'd call hype vibes," says Olympic shooter Seonaid McIntosh. "Because it's a smaller team than GB, we all know each other and want everyone else to have success. That's a really lovely culture and environment to be in."

Perhaps the greatest testimony to that atmosphere is not from those who were born and raised in Scotland but rather from those who choose to identify as Scots.

Take wrestler Christelle Lemofack. She competed for Cameroon at Glasgow 2014 but enjoyed the experience so much that she never went home. In Birmingham, she represented Scotland.

"I've made a life here and Scotland gave me that opportunity, so I feel like I have to give something back," she said before the last Games. "I've dreamed about this and now it's come true. I have to fight for my new flag."

Lemofack might not have the ginger hair that Olympic judoka Sarah Adlington boasts as part of her credentials to compete for Scotland, but elements of their stories are the same.

"You can't choose where you were born, but you can choose where you live and I've chosen to live my whole adult life in Scotland," says the 2014 Commonwealth gold medallist. "I feel Scottish, my coaches and team-mates are Scottish and I wouldn't want to compete for anyone else."

This article was originally published on 27 July 2022.

title: Man Utd bring in Leicester goalkeeper Leitzig
description: Manchester United sign goalkeeper Janina Leitzig from Leicester City for an undisclosed fee.
fullText:
Manchester United have signed goalkeeper Janina Leitzig from Leicester City for an undisclosed fee.

The 27-year-old becomes their second signing of the summer following the arrival of defender Andrea Medina.

It is believed the former Germany youth international has signed a three-year deal at United after they triggered the release clause in her Leicester contract, which was renewed in 2025.

Leitzig has been at Leicester for three years, initially on a season-long loan from Bayern Munich, where she became a regular starter.

She leaves having made almost 70 appearances in all competitions but could not save Leicester from Women's Super League relegation last season.

"It is a real honour to be a Manchester United player," said Leitzig.

"I'm ready to bring all of my experience of competing at the highest level to help the team to have a successful season.

"I am joining a really excellent group of goalkeepers. Everyone has told me about the great environment that they have created.

"I cannot wait to push all together to maintain the high performance standards that this club deserves."

Leitzig has been a long-term target for United and BBC Sport first reported in 2023 that they had made contact with the German goalkeeper while on loan at Leicester.

She will wear the number 25 shirt at Manchester United.

Later on Friday, Chelsea confirmed the signing of England youth international Nelly Las from Leicester City on a four-year deal.

The 18-year-old, who can play as a winger or a full-back, spent the second half of last season on loan at Ipswich Town.

Chelsea paid an undisclosed release clause fee for Las, who joined Leicester in 2024 and has made 23 appearances in all competitions for the club.

Las, who is bilingual in English and Slovak, came through Leicester's academy and has represented England U17s, U19s and U20s.

"It feels absolutely amazing. It's something you dream of when you start football, to sign for a team like Chelsea and to reach a level like this," said Las.

"I have been watching this team achieve success growing up, and to be here and signing for this club now, I have no words."

Meanwhile, Leicester are continuing their rebuild and have made Sarah Mayling's loan move from Aston Villa a permanent transfer.

The full-back joins on a three-year deal having spent eight years at Villa across two spells, as well as enjoying time in their youth academy.

She notched up over 100 appearances for Villa and becomes Leicester's second signing this summer.

title: England amputee team's World Cup dream on hold
description: Former head coach Scott Rogers has said it is "criminal" that England men's amputee football team could miss the 2026 World Cup due to a lack of funding.
fullText:
England's men's amputee football team could miss the upcoming World Cup in Mexico because of a lack of funding - a prospect the team's former head coach Scott Rogers called "criminal".

The team, who are the reigning Nations League champions, have set a GoFundMe target of £50,000 to attend November's tournament.

"I see how hard they [the players] work, I see how hard the staff work, I see the sacrifices they make and the families make as well," Rogers told BBC Breakfast.

"To get to this point now and not be able to go potentially, it's criminal really."

The Football Association funds other para national teams, but funding for the amputee programme was cut in 2006.

The England Amputee Football Association has since set up as a charity and it relies on donations and volunteers to support its men's and women's teams, along with a junior pathway.

FA representatives shadowed the men's amputee team at the 2022 World Cup and subsequently made a funding offer, but it fell short of what they felt was needed.

"Our funding model is we come on the television and people donate, and we are so grateful for that - we would love to be able to thank everyone individually for that - but it's not a funding model that is sustainable," Rogers added.

"We have a good relationship with the FA, but the problem is at the moment the information that we are getting back from them is there isn't the funding available to be able to bring amputee football under the FA's umbrella."

In the 2024-25 season, the FA generated a total turnover of £516m with an operating profit of £6m.

Meanwhile, England's men's team earned £21.5m in prize money for finishing third in this summer's World Cup.

"It's crazy. We're kind of battling against the system," said goalkeeper Thomas Atkinson.

"A lot of the teams we are competing against are full-time professionals, they are getting paid daily by clubs and the governing body, their national team fully supports them in everything they do.

"We're definitely not one of those teams."

The team have currently raised £32,427 of their £50,000 goal.

"We're playing as a hobby in a sense. We're having to pay to play whereas they're getting paid to play," Atkinson added.

"I'm not even asking to get paid to play football, I just think we as an organisation, as England – one of the biggest countries in football – shouldn't be having our national team players having to pay to attend tournaments. It's crazy, isn't it?"

An FA spokesperson said: "The England amputee team is currently independent from the FA.

"We continue to work closely with the England Amputee Football Association to support, identify and help deliver their key priorities over the coming season, and the continued development of amputee football in England."

title: Chelsea agree deal to sign Palace defender Lacroix
description: Chelsea agree deal to sign France defender Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace after two impressive seasons.
fullText:
Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix is set to join Chelsea on a long-term contract after the clubs reached agreement on a deal for the player.

BBC Sport reported on Tuesday that both clubs had held positive talks over a move for the France international, with Palace seeking about £60m for the centre-back.

An agreement has now been reached between the two clubs, with personal terms not believed to be an issue.

Lacroix is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours before signing a long-term contract, understood to run until 2032.

The agreement between the two London clubs has been negotiated at ownership level.

The 26-year-old was a regular under Oliver Glasner last season, making 55 appearances in all competitions as Palace won the Uefa Conference League, the club's first major European trophy.

He also featured in Palace's Community Shield victory over Liverpool and helped the Eagles secure another strong Premier League campaign.

Lacroix's performances earned him a place in France's squad for the 2026 World Cup. He made three appearances during the tournament, including starts against Norway and England in the third-place play-off, as Les Bleus finished fourth.

Palace signed Lacroix from Bundesliga side Wolfsburg in August 2024 for an initial fee of £15.5m, with a further £2.6m in potential add-ons.

He has gone on to establish himself as one of the Premier League's most consistent central defenders.

Chelsea have targeted Lacroix after two impressive seasons in English football.

During the 2025-26 Premier League campaign, he was the only player to record at least 50 tackles (60), 200 duels won (204) and 250 clearances (252).

At 6ft 4in, Lacroix combines aerial strength with exceptional recovery pace. Since arriving from Wolfsburg in 2024, he has ranked among the five fastest centre-backs in the Premier League, recording a top speed of 35.81km/h (22.3mph).

That athleticism is reflected in his defensive numbers. Across the past two Premier League seasons, Lacroix recorded the best success rate in one-on-one defensive situations among players to face at least 50 such duels, winning possession 50.5% of the time.

Lacroix is also tactically versatile. Comfortable in both a back four and a back three, he spent two seasons playing in Oliver Glasner's three-man defence at Crystal Palace but has also shown he can operate effectively in a more conventional back four.

That adaptability offers Chelsea additional options, with head coach Xabi Alonso having used both systems during his coaching career.

title: Opetaia sues IBF to return cruiserweight world title
description: Boxer Jai Opetaia starts legal action in the United States to try to force the IBF to hand back the cruiserweight world title.
fullText:
Boxer Jai Opetaia has started legal action in the United States to force the IBF to hand back the cruiserweight world title.

The Australian claims the sanctioning body acted unlawfully when it stripped him of his belt following his first fight with promotional outfit Zuffa Boxing.

Opetaia filed a lawsuit in the US District Court for the District of Nevada seeking to have his title reinstated, recover damages and legal costs, and prevent the IBF from naming another cruiserweight champion while the litigation continues.

The IBF declined to comment, with a spokesperson telling BBC Sport: "We will release a statement when it is appropriate."

The 19-page complaint - obtained by BBC Sport - claims rival governing bodies have discouraged champions from facing him, citing David Benavidez's decision not to pursue a fight after Opetaia was stripped and alleging the WBC threatened to strip Noel Mikaelian if he agreed to face the Australian instead.

"The conspirators and, most recently, the WBC have taken steps to freeze out Jai from other future bouts," the lawsuit says.

The complaint also names representatives from sanction bodies the WBC, WBA and WBO - BBC Sport has contacted them for comment.

Opetaia stripped of IBF title over Zuffa belt bout

What is Zuffa Boxing and can it shake up the sport?

The case centres on the fallout from 31-year-old Opetaia's decision to sign with Zuffa Boxing, the new promotion launched by UFC president Dana White and Saudi Arabian-owned Sela and American company TKO.

Opetaia's first fight under the promotion came against Brandon Glanton in Las Vegas in March. His IBF world title was due to be defended on the same night that Zuffa Boxing introduced its inaugural cruiserweight championship belt.

According to the complaint, the IBF initially approved those arrangements, accepted a $73,000 (£54,000) sanctioning fee and appointed an official to oversee the contest, before withdrawing its sanctioning less than 48 hours before fight night.

The lawsuit argues the IBF later treated the contest as a title unification because a Zuffa Boxing belt was also being contested.

Opetaia disputes that interpretation, arguing the organisation had already accepted the Zuffa belt was merely a "trophy or token of recognition", rather than the championship of another sanctioning body. He says there was no legitimate basis for the IBF to reverse its position.

The filing says Opetaia was "placed in an impossible position" by the late decision, forcing him to choose between withdrawing from a contest he had spent months preparing for and losing "his seven-figure compensation", or proceeding with the fight and "risk being stripped of his championship".

Opetaia chose to box, defeating Glanton by unanimous decision, before the IBF subsequently vacated his title.

The lawsuit further alleges the IBF's actions were "the product of coordinated, industry-wide collusion designed to penalise Jai for signing with Zuffa Boxing and to deter other athletes from doing the same".

There is precedent of a fighter being reinstated as a world champion following legal action.

In 2004, the WBC was forced into liquidation after losing a £17m legal battle against former champion Graciano Rocchigiani.

Rocchigiani won the WBC's vacant light-heavyweight title in March 1998 after it had been relinquished by Roy Jones Jr.

But Jones decided he wanted to keep the belt and the WBC reinstated him as champion in June 1998.

In addition to the compensation, the WBC was ordered to recognise Rocchigiani as champion from 1998-2000.

Zuffa Boxing launched in June 2025 with ambitions of challenging the established promoters and sanctioning bodies that dominate the sport.

The promotion currently recognises eight weight divisions, with one Zuffa champion crowned in each category.

White has previously stated that Zuffa Boxing will not rely on the traditional world titles awarded by the WBA, WBA, WBO and IBF.

White has also expressed his desire to make changes to Muhammad Ali Boxing Reform Act, the 2000 US law introduced to protect boxers' rights and prevent conflicts of interest and monopolistic practices within the sport.

Changes to the legislation could potentially allow a Zuffa championship belt to be recognised as a legitimate world title, reducing the promotion's reliance on the existing sanctioning bodies.

Zuffa Boxing made its first major statement in February when it signed welterweight contender Conor Benn in a high-profile move away from Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Boxing.

Earlier this month, four-division world champion Shakur Stevenson became the latest major name to join Zuffa Boxing.

Stevenson currently holds the WBO lightweight title, although it remains unclear whether he will be stripped of the belt following his move.

Benn, meanwhile, is scheduled to challenge Ryan Garcia for the WBC welterweight title on 12 September.

American light-welterweight Richardson Hitchins vacated his IBF title after signing with Zuffa, while pound-for-pound star Oleksandr Usyk recently relinquished his WBA (Super), IBF and WBC titles and has been linked with a potential move to the promotion.

title: Messiah or papering over cracks? Klopp must sway doubters in Germany rebuild
description: Jurgen Klopp is a legend at his former clubs, but he will need to convince his critics if he is to succeed in his toughest managerial challenge yet.
fullText:
He was once hailed as Liverpool's footballing messiah. Now Jurgen Klopp has been asked to work miracles for his country.

Last month, Klopp watched on as a touchline TV pundit as Germany went out of the World Cup in a shock penalty shootout defeat by Paraguay.

The loss led head coach Julian Nagelsmann to resign and plunged German football into a full-scale identity crisis.

Just three weeks later, it is Klopp who has been tasked with picking up the pieces and restoring his country's once-famous winning mentality, signing a four-year deal to become head coach.

Assigned with leading the team through Euro 2028 and the 2030 World Cup, Klopp's first game in charge will be against the Netherlands on 24 September.

"The national team can unite us Germans like almost nothing else. That's precisely what makes this task so special for me," Klopp said.

A Champions League and Premier League winner with Liverpool and a two-time Bundesliga champion with Borussia Dortmund, the 59-year-old is already considered one of the greatest German managers.

Yet while many believe he is the perfect man for the national team job, the appointment has also sparked fierce debate in Germany.

For the German football association (DFB), securing Klopp's signature has been a priority since Nagelsmann resigned in the wake of the Paraguay defeat.

DFB president Bernd Neuendorf said Klopp "embodies passion, credibility, and the ability to inspire people".

"After Julian Nagelsmann's resignation, he was our unequivocal choice for the position of national team coach. That's why we pursued him relentlessly," Neuendorf added.

Klopp starts Germany reign by threatening to quit

Klopp has signed a deal until 2030 and will build his coaching team around former Liverpool assistants Pep Lijnders and Peter Krawietz.

Germany will hope the trio can do for them what they once did for the Premier League club and restore one of football's fallen giants to its former glory.

Few doubt Klopp has what it takes to breathe new life into the national team.

In a recent poll by Germany's leading football magazine Kicker, external, 80% of readers said they thought Klopp was the right choice.

Of the many criticisms of the German team in recent years, the most enduring have been a lack of winning mentality and a failure to bond with fans.

Klopp, who has spent his career talking about "mentality monsters" and became a cult hero at every club he has managed, would seem to be the perfect solution.

Speaking on the popular weekly football talk show Doppelpass, former Germany and Bayern Munich midfielder Stefan Effenberg said Klopp could bring a "new spirit of optimism".

For Borussia Dortmund chief executive Carsten Cramer, the new manager's influence may even go beyond sport.

"I think he embodies a lot of the things that our football and our country are missing right now," Cramer told Kicker.

Germany fans in need of hope as prospect of Klopp looms

'A joke' - how a 'terrible' VAR disallowed goal cost Germany

Yet not everyone is so enamoured of the new national team boss.

Klopp's reputation has suffered in Germany since he joined Red Bull as head of global soccer in 2024, in a move many fans saw as a betrayal.

German fans have long criticised Red Bull for its multi-club model and effective circumvention of the much-loved 50+1 rule, which guarantees supporter voting rights at German clubs.

In July, reports Klopp could continue to work as a brand ambassador for Red Bull after becoming Germany manager were met with outrage.

Former DFB president Theo Zwanziger told Frankfurter Allgemeine newspaper, external such a move would be "an absolute no-go", adding Red Bull "want to win power inside the sport".

Meanwhile, fan group Unsere Kurve said the DFB should not "kowtow to capital" by allowing Red Bull to keep Klopp on their books.

"Before hailing him as the Messiah, we should remember how much goodwill he has squandered, especially among Dortmund fans," the group's spokesperson Thomas Kessen told news agency SID.

Others have criticised the DFB's rush to hire Klopp without considering other candidates.

"It's obvious that he is number one, but when you see the delegation flying to New York, it seems a bit hectic. You have to ask: do they have any alternatives?" said 2014 World Cup winner Bastian Schweinsteiger as a pundit on ARD.

He added Klopp could only be a "band-aid", as Germany's current woes run much deeper than the dugout.

The German men's national team is currently at its lowest ebb in decades, having failed to reach the last 16 at the past three World Cups.

Many, including Klopp himself, have argued for root-and-branch reform at all levels of the game.

"I have said many times that it's not just about the head coach," the incoming Germany manager told MagentaTV earlier this month.

"German football as a whole is facing a turning point, we have to change some fundamental things."

For Klopp, the rebuild will begin in September when Germany open their Nations League campaign against the Netherlands, their traditional rivals.

The real test for the 59-year-old will come in two years' time, when the UK and Ireland host Euro 2028.

In a twist of fate, that tournament could see Klopp make an emotional return to the city of Liverpool.

Though Anfield is not a venue at Euro 2028, Klopp's Germany could end up playing at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium.
