fullText:
MARIETTA, Georgia, July 22 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump rallied supporters in Georgia on Wednesday to press for stricter nationwide voting requirements, leaning into his election-security message that some Republicans worry could hurt them in the state's competitive U.S. Senate race.

Trump's ‌speech in the Atlanta suburbs follows months of attacks on Georgia's election system, which he has criticized since his 2020 loss in the ‌state. So far this year, the president has questioned Georgia's voting system at least nine times during public events and interviews, according to a Reuters review.

In a June podcast, Trump falsely ​said the 2020 election in Georgia was rigged. Days later, during a telephone rally for a Republican gubernatorial candidate, Trump said: "Our elections are corrupt."

On Wednesday, Trump said some Republican victories in the state were "not going to be that easy with the cheating and everything else going on."

He urged supporters to call Senate Majority Leader John Thune and pressure him to push through his administration's election bill imposing stricter voting requirements nationwide.

The Georgia rally was Trump's first campaign event since a ‌prime-time White House speech last week in which he ⁠questioned the security of U.S. elections.

The president traveled to Marietta in a politically competitive part of the state after attending a ceremony for four U.S. service members killed in recent Iranian attacks in the Middle East.

Some Georgia Republicans worry ⁠Trump's rhetoric could backfire by discouraging turnout in November's midterm elections, when control of Congress will be at stake.

"President Trump's supporters are less likely to turn out when he casts doubt on the validity on the election process," said Eric Johnson, the former Republican leader of the Georgia Senate and state chair for RightCount, a ​conservative ​group that defends state-run elections.

TRUMP PRESSES ELECTION SECURITY AS ISSUE FOR MIDTERMS

The 2020 election ​remains a central focus for Trump, particularly in Georgia where administration ‌officials have launched investigations into the handling of the vote.

After losing Georgia to Democrat Joe Biden, Trump pressured the state's top election official to "find" enough votes to overturn the result, and repeatedly challenged the election's legitimacy. Multiple recounts confirmed Biden's victory.

The issue of election security has featured in the state's competitive Senate race, where Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff is running for reelection against Republican U.S. Representative Mike Collins. A Fox News poll in July showed Ossoff leading Collins by 13 percentage points among registered voters.

Ossoff has challenged Trump's voting claims and called him the "world's most famous sore loser." Collins has backed ‌the president's push for stricter voting requirements and told CNN in June that he ​believes Trump won the 2020 race in Georgia.

On Wednesday, Trump cast Collins as a reliable ally ​who supported tax cuts for Georgians and would bring federal investment ​to the state. The president called Ossoff a "terrible" senator and repeated his claim that some progressive members of the Democratic ‌Party are "communists."

Collins said he skipped Trump's rally on Wednesday in ​order to cast votes in Washington, a ​move Trump praised as he urged voters to support the Republican in November.

Georgia law already requires voters to show identification to vote, and the state's Republican leaders also passed voting rules after the 2020 election that limited ballot drop boxes and absentee ballots.

Several Republican voters interviewed at ​Trump's rally on Wednesday said, however, that they still ‌do not trust the voting process.

"Republicans are frustrated because they don't see the reason to vote because they know there's going ​to be cheating," said Rita Rohrssen, an 80-year-old retired registered nurse from Woodstock, Georgia.

title: More than 24 states sue Trump administration after it put conditions on receiving disaster funding
description: More than two dozen states on Thursday sued the Trump administration for requiring them to comply with election and immigration conditions to receive billions of dollars in federal funding for disaste...
fullText:
BOSTON (AP) — More than two dozen states on Thursday sued the Trump administration for requiring them to comply with election and immigration conditions to receive billions of dollars in federal funding for disasters.

The lawsuit, filed in Rhode Island and challenging Federal Emergency Management Agency and Department of Homeland Security policies, argued that the administration is requiring states to change their elections systems and help DHS with immigration enforcement. The conditions would also allow DHS to terminate grants at any time and for any reason.

"Once again, the Trump Administration is threatening to jeopardize public safety by unlawfully withholding billions in critical funding and once again, they won't get away with it," Rhode Island Attorney General Peter Neronha said. "This Administration is using the safety of Americans as collateral by attempting to bully the states into relinquishing their constitutional right to enact policies and laws that best serve their residents."

The states argue putting conditions on congressionally appropriated funding violates the Administrative Procedure Act and the U.S. Constitution's spending clause.

In a statement, a spokesperson for FEMA called the lawsuit an example of "partisan pushback" and said they expected "these left-wing politicians to oppose common-sense measures designed to protect election security and safeguard the integrity of American democracy."

"Election security is national security, and protecting our critical infrastructure remains a top priority for the Trump Administration," they said. "Concerns over voting processes, data security, and registration practices have made it clear that action is required."

The lawsuit is one of scores that have challenged the Trump administration over its repeated effort to browbeat mostly Democratic states into complying with its priorities to get billions of dollars in federal funding. The strategy has been used on everything from education funding to domestic violence grants to highway funding.

The courts have repeatedly found this strategy to be unlawful and unconstitutional. A ruling last year barred the administration from putting conditions on other FEMA funding, and a second ruling this year blocked the administration from redirecting DHS funding away from states not seen as supportive of its agenda.

"The States face losing billions of dollars in federal funding, are being put in a position of relinquishing their sovereign right to decide how to use their own police officers, are at risk of losing the trust built between local law enforcement and immigrant communities, and will have to scale back, reconsider, or cancel ongoing transportation projects," U.S. District Judge John McConnell Jr. wrote last year, when he barred the Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy from cutting off transportation funds to states that did not comply with immigration enforcement actions.

The latest lawsuit argues the administration is attempting to apply some of the same conditions on 2026 funding, as it failed to do with funding last year.

Among the requirements being challenged in Thursday's lawsuit is that states change their elections systems. They must transition to paper-ballot systems, conduct a manual audit of voting systems, reconcile voters and verify the citizenship of every registered voter in the state's voter databases.

If states fail to comply, they risk losing at least 20% of their Homeland Security Grant Program funding. That money is used to fund measures to protect citizens from cyberattacks and terrorism.

"The Trump Administration is holding critical funding for homeland security and disaster response hostage in their latest attempt to take over our elections and perpetuate baseless conspiracy theories," Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, one of the plaintiffs in the lawsuit, said in a statement.

Since his 2020 presidential election loss to Democrat Joe Biden, Trump has groundlessly claimed mail voting is rife with fraud and has launched a federal investigation into that year's vote, even though repeated audits and investigations, including ones run by Republicans, found it was free of widespread fraud. Trump also has said he wants to "take over" election administration in Democratic areas.

title: WATCH: ‘Shocking’ Ben Franklin smear leaves Smithsonian chief with ‘no regrets’
description: A Heritage Foundation expert called a Smithsonian exhibit "shocking" for suggesting Benjamin Franklin may have used electroshock on enslaved people.
fullText:
The director of the country's premier American history museum said she has no regrets about any of the museum's exhibits during her tenure after an expert confronted her with a "shocking" display that he said smeared Founding Father Benjamin Franklin.

Smithsonian National Museum of American History Director Anthea Hartig faced intense questioning from lawmakers during two Capitol Hill hearings this week. The hearings followed a White House Domestic Policy Council report accusing the museum of using taxpayer dollars and its status as a world-renowned institution to advance a "radical activist ideology."

During a House hearing Tuesday, Heritage Foundation expert Mike Gonzalez testified that a multiyear special exhibit, "The Electric Dr. Franklin," included a display that "pondered whether he had ever done experiments, electrical electroshock on indentured servants or slaves."

Watch: Smithsonian Director Pressed On Woke Exhibits: 'Is Mickey Mouse Racist?'

Gonzalez testified that the display included this suggestion "without producing any evidence whatsoever," which he called "shocking."

"Why smear a Founding Father such as Ben Franklin by pondering such a really bizarre thing," Gonzalez asked.

Immediately after Gonzalez's testimony, Rep. Brian Jack, R-Ga., confronted Hartig, saying, "We've heard a lot of concerning examples as just referenced. Do you have any regrets in your tenure thus far [about] some of the exhibits that have been displayed? Do you regret any of the exhibits and, if so, which?"

Hartig answered, "I am incredibly proud of the work we've done, but we are imperfect, and we surely have made mistakes. But I don't have any regrets."

Jack pressed further, asking, "Which mistakes would you say you've made?"

"There are always factual errors," Hartig responded.

"One of my favorite, currently," she added, "is that one of our volunteers has pointed out that we've been mislabeling a coin in the American Presidency exhibit for years, and we were, of course, you know, slightly embarrassed about that, but we fixed it."

Hartig became director of the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History in February 2019. The Benjamin Franklin exhibit opened to the public in 2021 and remained on display through 2025.

'The View' Co-host Whines Smithsonian Hearings Are About Trump Administration Not Wanting To Pay Reparations

The museum has a webpage containing expanded material from the exhibit. The site states that "researchers also used people as conductors to determine how far an electrical charge might travel, and if electrical effects would fade with distance.

"Franklin wrote about experiments in which he took shocks and used family and friends in these ways, although he seldom identified who in particular assisted him. Indentured servants and enslaved people in his household could also have been used, although we may never know for certain."

A sweeping new White House report concluded that the Smithsonian Institution's National Museum of American History has become a taxpayer-backed institution of "ideological capture" and "extreme political activism."

According to the 162-page "Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History" report, delivered on America's 250th birthday, NMAH treats the American story as a political tool rather than a shared national inheritance.

The White House Domestic Policy Council wrote that the "Smithsonian Institution, and the National Museum of American History in particular, under its current leadership and current interpretive ideology, cannot be trusted to tell America's story honestly and in a way that is inspiring, unifying, and worthy of our great republic."

Further, the report said that "by the intention and at the direction of current Museum and Smithsonian leadership, NMAH has become subject to institutional capture by a radical, activist ideology that is fundamentally opposed to telling the noble, honest story of the great country we know and love."

Watch: Smithsonian History Museum Director Stumbles Over Basic Questions On Sex: 'I'm Not Sure'

During her testimony Tuesday, Hartig said "the Smithsonian takes the concerns raised in the White House Domestic Policy Counsel's report seriously, and as we continue to fact-check the report, we unwaveringly attest that it does not fairly or accurately characterize the full body of work at the museum."

She added that "there is always room for improvement, but I also know the beauty and the inspiration and the expertise that lies in our collections, our exhibits and our programming."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Smithsonian Institution, the National Museum of American History and Gonzalez for additional comment.

title: Watch an orca ram a sunfish so hard that the fish explodes
description: Scientists captured video of orcas ramming into sunfish with such force that the fish exploded. The behavior may be for fun as well as for feeding, they report.
fullText:
How hard do you have to ram a fish to make it explode? Ask an orca.

Barreling into large, heavy fish with enough force to blast them into instant chum is a previously unknown collaborative feeding strategy among orcas, scientifically called Orcinus orca, also known as killer whales.

But in 2024 and 2025, divers captured underwater video of two such events in the Mexican Pacific Ocean and in the Gulf of California. The footage suggests that the brutal body slamming may be in service of a meal — or perhaps a form of play for the orcas, researchers reported Thursday in the journal Frontiers in Ethology.

"I filmed the first event several years ago and couldn't believe what I was witnessing," said lead study author Kathryn Ayres, a research scientist for the marine conservation nonprofit Beneath the Waves and the first to capture orcas' high-speed ramming on video.

Ayres studies sharks but observing orcas that preyed on sharks in the Gulf of California sparked her interest in killer whale behavior. She filmed the encounter on July 29, 2024, while diving as an ocean safari tour guide with the group Latitude Encounters, near the coast of San José del Cabo in the Mexican state of Baja California Sur.

"The cooperative ramming behaviour itself wasn't entirely new to me, as I had previously observed similar coordinated ramming during a hunt involving a whale shark," she told CNN in an email.

Orcas have also made headlines in recent years for teaming up to ram and sink yachts in waters near Spain and Portugal.

"What was unique in this case was the outcome," Ayres said. "Seeing the sunfish fragment into countless pieces was unlike anything I had encountered before." Her astonishment was audible as she recorded the ramming episode. "Oh, god!" she repeatedly exclaimed.

A second video of orcas holding and then ramming a sunfish was filmed by another tour operator in the Gulf of California in September. Both incidents demonstrated teamwork; one orca held a sharptail sunfish, scientifically named Masturus lanceolatus, by its tail, while another orca swam toward the fish at high speed. Moments before impact, the restraining orca let go, and its partner slammed into the sunfish like a freight train hitting a watermelon. Young orcas then gobbled up fish fragments that drifted through the water as their elders tore into what was left of the sunfish's corpse.

Sharptail sunfish, or molas, are among the heaviest fish in the world, weighing more than 4,000 pounds (1,800 kilograms) and measuring up to 10 feet (3 meters) long.

Orcas often coordinate their attacks in pairs or groups when they target large prey. However, this torpedolike body slam and subsequent fish explosion had never been observed before and was "an incredible behavior to see," said Monika Wieland Shields, director of the Orca Behavior Institute. Shields was not involved in the new research.

"I have never heard of anything similar to this occurring, so it is indeed a newly documented behavior as far as I know," Shields told CNN in an email.

Though all orcas belong to a single species, their diets vary widely depending on where they live. Orcas' prey may include fish, seals, belugas, narwhals, baleen whales or porpoises, and can require specialized feeding tactics — including, it seems, high-impact fragmentation.

"I think that as we continue to observe orcas more closely around the world," Shields added, "we will continue to discover novel hunting and feeding behaviors, especially among lesser-studied populations."

Ramming the sunfish and causing them to explode could help orca calves and juveniles get more of the remains, according to the study. What's more, working together strengthens social bonds in orcas, as do shared meals. An exploded sunfish spread out in the water in thousands of pieces is certainly easier to share, offering another possible explanation for this practice.

But orcas are also known to play with newly dead food. Some orcas in Puget Sound off Washington state have worn dead salmon as hats. Others drape seal intestines over their fins or take turns tossing sea lion pelts into the air, Shields said.

"We've also seen interactions with many other objects including bull kelp, driftwood, and crab pots," she said, "In many of these cases there doesn't seem to be a functional reason for these behaviors other than play."

In other words, it's possible that orcas body-slam sunfish purely for entertainment. Ayres noted a large wound on the fish's body before the impact, which hinted that the orcas feasted on the creature before slamming it to pieces.

"They had already consumed the sunfish's internal organs, which are the most nutrient-rich parts of the prey," Ayres told CNN in an email. "This suggests that causing the sunfish to explode may not have served an immediate feeding purpose and could have just been for fun."

The sunfish's flattened body structure is unusual in large fish and could make them more likely to fly apart after a high-speed orca impact compared with other types of fish, Ayres added.

"Their bodies are laterally compressed," she explained. "Once the nutrient-rich internal organs have been removed, the remaining tissues may be more accessible to rupture under high-impact ramming."

But for now, she cautioned, this is only a hypothesis.

"We haven't seen this type of prey fragmentation described in other sunfish species," she said, "so it's difficult to know whether it reflects something unique about the anatomy of Masturus lanceolatus, the specific behaviour of these orcas, or a combination of both."

Mindy Weisberger is a science writer and media producer whose work has appeared in Live Science, Scientific American and How It Works magazine. She is the author of "Rise of the Zombie Bugs: The Surprising Science of Parasitic Mind-Control" (Hopkins Press).

title: Nearly 150,000 mail ballots rejected in California' primary despite efforts to count every vote
description: Nearly 150,000 California voters had their mail-in ballots rejected for the state's June primary, a spike from recent elections even as the state attempts to make voting easier with the goal of boosti...
fullText:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Nearly 150,000 California voters had their mail-in ballots rejected for the state's June primary, a spike from recent elections even as the state attempts to make voting easier with the goal of boosting participation and counting every ballot.

California has become notorious for its ponderously slow vote counts that can drag on for weeks and sometimes longer, largely the result of multiple changes over the years that were intended to increase turnout but have done little to achieve that. Among the changes: Every voter receives a mail-in ballot that can arrive at an election office seven days late and still be counted, provided the envelope is postmarked by Election Day.

Yet even with that generous week-long window, the primary driver of the higher rejection numbers is late-arriving ballots, according to data compiled by the secretary of state's office. Voting experts suspect the main problem is postmarks on ballots that came after Election Day, making them ineligible to be counted. The culprit could be U.S. Postal Service changes that might affect the timing of when postmarks are applied.

According to state data, 148,241 mail ballots were rejected in the June election, or a rate of 1.73% of all mail ballots.

In raw numbers, that's up from the 2024 primary, when 108,982 mail ballots were rejected, or a 1.56% rate. In 2022, 105,818 mail ballots were voided during the primary, or a rate similar to 2024.

Lateness accounted for 93,479 rejected ballots in June, by far the largest category for disqualifying a ballot. That was up from about 70,000 in the 2022 primary and about 76,000 in the 2024 primary, though turnout in those elections was smaller compared to last June.

Kim Alexander, president of the nonpartisan California Voter Foundation, said the jump in rejected ballots because of lateness is a major concern that — along with postal procedures — might also be connected to a late surge in ballots in June. Many voters waited until the final days to make a decision in a wide-open and chaotic race for governor.

"Ballots rejected due to lateness are caused primarily to being postmarked too late to count, not because they arrived too late to count," Alexander wrote in an email.

Rejection rates have fluctuated over time, but the growing number of those set aside for lateness compared to recent elections "does really demand the question why this is happening," said Mindy Romero, director of the Center for Inclusive Democracy, a nonpartisan research group.

In January, a group of mostly Democratic U.S. senators sent a letter to the U.S. Postal Service, alarmed that mail-processing changes might affect postmark dates for mail-in ballots during an election year that will determine control of Congress.

Updated agency policy says postmarks might not indicate the first day the Postal Service received the mail, but rather the day it was handled in one of its processing centers. Those centers are increasingly likely to be further away from certain communities because of recent consolidations within the Postal Service, which could further delay postmarks.

On Thursday, two Wisconsin Democrats, U.S. Sen. Tammy Baldwin and Gov. Tony Evers, called on the Postal Service to address delays that caused hundreds of ballots to arrive after Election Day in the state in April. In June, a federal judge halted President Donald Trump's executive order that sought to create a federal voter list and limit who can receive a mail ballot.

Earlier this year, California election officials urged voters to send their mail ballots early, warning that Postal Service changes could lead to slower mail service.

In California, the highest mail ballot rejection rate in June — 3.52% — was in Tulare County, in the agriculture-heavy Central Valley. It was followed by Alpine County, south of Lake Tahoe, and Merced County, also in the Central Valley, which both notched a 3.36% rejection rate.

Nearly 44,000 ballots were set aside because the voter's signature didn't match the one on record with county officials. Over 8,300 ballots were rejected because there was no signature on the returned ballot envelope.

In 743 cases, the voter had already cast a ballot, so the mail ballot was voided. Other reasons for rejection included a ballot being missing from the return envelope, or multiple ballots were sent back in a single envelope.

The data didn't break down the uncounted ballots by party registration.

Florida, Texas and other large population states quickly wrap up vote counting, while California is a national laggard.

After the June primary, President Donald Trump seized on California's reputation as the national slowpoke in vote counting to renew his long-standing criticism of the state's elections, while the Republican's Department of Justice launched an investigation into Los Angeles County's elections.

There is no indication of any widespread problems with mail voting, which has gained in popularity among Democrats and Republicans alike. A report by the Brookings Institution published in 2025 found that the number of cases of mail voting fraud was minuscule — about four cases per 10 million mail ballots.

title: Vyner braced for eye-opening Wrexham popularity in US
description: Wrexham defender Zak Vyner is looking forward to see for himself how popular the Welsh club are in the United States.
fullText:
Wrexham defender Zak Vyner is looking forward to see how popular the Welsh club are in the United States for himself.

The Championship club, who recently faced Wisla Krakow in Poland and Manchester United in Finland, have travelled to the US for three games.

Wrexham's previous two tours of America have attracted huge crowds due to their global profile under owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac and the success of the Welcome to Wrexham documentary series.

"It's going to be a lot of hard work, but it'll be a great experience for me to get a taste of it," Vyner said.

"I only sort of get a taste of the American fans through social media and when I signed and the amount of love that I have got from them.

"In that way, I haven't actually seen it first-hand yet, so I'm really excited.

"We had the two European friendlies, so you got the taste of how Wrexham travels and the fans over there in the cities that we went to, and I was taken aback.

"The lads say America's ten times that, so it will be an eye-opener and good fun.

"I've spoken to the lads from the previous tours and the amazing places that they go to just to sort of pick their brains about what the games are like and playing against top opposition."

Wrexham, preparing for a second successive season in the Championship, meet Leeds in Tampa on Sunday, 26 July before facing Liverpool in New York four days later.

Their final pre-season game is against Sunderland on Sunday, 2 August in Philadelphia and Vyner is looking forward to make an impression on tour.

"I'm ready to go, I feel good, I feel fit," Vyner added.

"These tours, and pre-season in general, are for everyone to essentially give the manager a headache.

"I'm looking to do that and hopefully have some more games, get some more minutes, get myself fitter and just be ready for the season."

Vyner, 29, joined Wrexham from Championship rivals Bristol City for an undisclosed fee during the January transfer window.

He had a toe injury when he joined and was then thrust into action in central midfield. He missed the final five games of the season with a groin injury.

"I went away in the summer and there's a lot more to come," Vyner said.

"When you move to a new club, and it's the first time I've done that on a permanent basis, it is about getting to grips with everything off pitch as well.

"There's a whole bunch of stuff that goes on behind the scenes that people don't really see.

"Just bedding into a new place, new club and a new changing room, is a big jump.

"I feel now a lot closer to the lads and everyone's been great, but getting a lot closer naturally and getting to know each other's personalities, playing styles, everything, takes a bit of time.

"I'm ready to go and there's a lot more to come."

title: Socceroos star allegedly tests positive for cocaine after speeding
description: Socceroos World Cup star Cristian Volpato allegedly tests positive for cocaine after being twice caught for speeding in Sydney.
fullText:
Socceroos World Cup star Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine after police twice stopped him for speeding in Sydney on the same night.

The 22-year-old Australia midfielder was stopped in a BMW Coupe on the Anzac Bridge at 11:05pm local time on Thursday night after he was caught travelling between 86-94km/h in a 60km/h zone, police said.

He was subjected to a roadside breath test, which returned a negative result.

However, Volpato allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine when he was stopped two hours later for travelling at 109km/h in the same 60km/h zone.

New South Wales state police said Volpato was issued an infringement notice for excess speed, while his international driver's licence was suspended for six months - which means he cannot drive in New South Wales.

The police also said their inquiries will continue and a secondary sample of oral fluid was taken for further analysis.

Volpato played in three of Australia's four World Cup matches as they reached the round of 32, where they were knocked out by Egypt in a penalty shootout.

Having represented Italy at youth level, he switched allegiances to Australia in May just before the Socceroos announced their squad for the tournament.

Volpato has played at Serie A side Sassuolo since 2023 and he made 24 league appearances for the club as they finished 11th last season.

BBC Sport has approached Football Australia and Sassuolo for comment.

title: What's working - and what's not - for WSL fans?
description: BBC Sport spoke to fans of the Women's Super League and England Lionesses to learn about their experiences in the game and discuss what could be improved.
fullText:
"Attendance FC? That's your insult? You're jealous!"

Rachel Major regularly finds herself fending off jibes from rival fans towards Arsenal's growing attendances. A supporter of 20 years, she has enjoyed a prime seat at the club that is driving the growth of the women's game.

Last season, the Gunners averaged 34,000 at Emirates Stadium, almost four times the next highest average attendance which was set by Chelsea - and better than eight Premier League clubs., external

Arsenal's home crowds accounted for 41% of all supporters at WSL fixtures, a club success story, though one that raises questions about the overall supporter experience as both league and clubs strive to progress.

To investigate, BBC Sport asked fans how the game can keep existing followers engaged, captivate new supporters and inspire the next generation.

In January 2026, a YouGov study, external found 28.5m fans of WSL football globally, split equally by gender with almost half aged 18-34.

It is notably different from the men's game, which skews male and older.

"At a men's game, you feel like you're just a cog," says Donna Jones, a season ticket-holder at London City Lionesses. "The game doesn't care about the fans. In the women's game, the players and staff want to build a relationship."

Bankrolled by billionaire majority owner Michele Kang, London City are the only fully independent WSL club and averaged a home crowd of just under 3,000 at League One Bromley's Copperjax Community Stadium in their top-flight debut.

Their efforts to entice new supporters earned the Best Fan Engagement prize at the 2026 Women's Football Awards., external

"The club have done a fantastic job at creating an environment that's not just about the match," adds Jones. "They have different food options, a T-shirt cannon, foam fingers, player signings, a spin-the-wheel at half-time - there is so much.

"They are really trying to grow the fanbase."

The family-friendly hallmark of the women's game has been critical to its growth in England, whose back-to-back victories at the European Championships in 2022 and 2025 ignited an explosion of interest.

Pre-match activities planned for the Wembley fan park before England's fixture against Spain in April encouraged Mark Jenkins to take his six-year-old daughters to their first professional match.

"We did a lot of research in terms of what time to turn up and what would be going on - it was a really good atmosphere in the fan park," he tells BBC Sport. "[My daughters] enjoyed it and the first thing they said was, 'Can we do it again?'

"Women's sport is more accessible now. Eventually they will know the players' names and have posters on the wall just as I had."

The women's game has trialled a fan choice pilot, external over the past two seasons, permitting alcohol to be consumed in the stands.

Adopted by 18 clubs across the WSL and WSL2, it has been well received, with 70% of supporters now in favour, external of the initiative.

"It's absolutely brilliant," affirms Arsenal season ticket-holder Major. "People are better behaved.

"Before, you had 15 minutes to get in the queue, to buy a drink and then down it before you got in. That can promote irresponsible drinking."

The head of women's football at the Football Supporters' Association, Deborah Dilworth, says this is one of many strategies to enhance the matchday experience.

"The fan choice pilot is something that we've supported but this isn't the only part," she explains. "You need to look at food. You need to look at people going into the stadium, where they're walking, how comfortable they feel and how safe they feel."

With attendances increasing, there has been a drive to create separate seating areas to accommodate both avid match-goers and casual followers.

"As different seating sections have been distinguished, there has been a drive to make it clear as to where and what each ticket is," Dilworth explains.

"Home clubs need to have a vibrant section to create an atmosphere but equally there are new fans, neutrals and families."

WSL clubs to provide alcohol at games after trials

The biggest complaint from fans is scheduling.

In 2025-26, the WSL replaced the Sunday 18:45 kick-off time with more noon matches, but this also proved unpopular.

"For an away day it's horrible," explains Arsenal fan Major. "You've got fans leaving at three o'clock in the morning or you're going the night before and having to pay for a hotel."

The revised time also clashes with grassroots football, played widely on a Sunday morning. It is a barrier for the younger generation to attend games.

Regular breaks throughout the season are an issue too. Earlier this year, former England defender Anita Asante suggested extended gaps between league games hampers momentum and rhythm for fans.

Another complaint from supporters is accessibility.

While Premier League-level grounds like Emirates Stadium and Everton's Goodison Park are well equipped, smaller venues are less accommodating.

Jones, a wheelchair user, was frustrated by the lack of Blue Badge parking information when trying to attend London City's away trip to Tottenham Hotspur.

"A lot of the issues I experience are with communication," she says. "Every club has an accessibility section on their website but for Tottenham it is only for the Tottenham Hotspur stadium, not Brisbane Road [where Tottenham women play]."

Jones told BBC Sport the onus was on her to seek further information via email, to which she received a reply stating Blue Badge parking had sold out. Only after she spoke to Tottenham's disability co-ordinator did she learn the venue did not have Blue Badge parking as it was in a residential area.

To compound matters, the wheelchair accessible allocation was on the opposite side of the ground to the away section, leaving Jones isolated.

Tottenham Hotspur told BBC Sport information for the venue is available on the website via the 'Ask Spurs' chatbot. However, after an internal investigation, they are making improvements.

Brisbane Road-specific guidance has since been added to their event day accessible parking section on 'Ask Spurs', while a matchday-specific guide is in the works.

A spokesperson for the club confirmed: "We're working on a full Brisbane Road matchday guide for the website for next season to give parity with our Tottenham Hotspur Stadium information."

Smaller stadiums pose further difficulties given lower quality facilities on offer, larger distances to travel and more complex journeys to navigate.

Major, who travels home and away with Arsenal, highlighted unfavourable conditions when visiting West Ham's Chigwell Construction Stadium, shared with National League club Dagenham & Redbridge.

"There are no seats so if there's someone who is less able to stand, if they're old, if they're injured, if they're disabled, it's not a good experience," she says.

"The whole stand is not covered. It's not a problem in the summer, but [in winter] people are out in the rain."

For most WSL teams, a key strategy to grow their fanbase is to capture the interest of fans already invested in the men's side.

Manchester City and Arsenal held parades at the end of 2025-26 to celebrate the successes of their women's, men's and academy sides.

Gunners fan Major highlights the use of "real fans" in promotional campaigns as an example of the club's ongoing efforts to foster a collective identity.

There are pitfalls to aligning too closely however, as Reading and Charlton Athletic have previously discovered. In 2024, the Royals were demoted from tier two to tier five after the club fell into financial difficulty, while the Addicks were disbanded entirely in 2007 after the men's team suffered relegation.

Next season, Charlton will play top-flight football for the first time since that era.

It means Dilworth at the Football Supporters Association is cautious about clubs simply seeking to "copy and paste from the men's game".

"Are there opportunities to do things differently?" she asks. "Everybody's desperately trying to do the right thing. Innovation is key but not to potentially compromise what people really love about the game."

Another sticking point with the 'one club' approach is the home venue.

"There's something really powerful in the narrative around a stadium for both men's and women's first teams," says Dilworth.

"However, if then beneath that there is still a tone and a culture of the primacy to the men, that's when you run into difficulties."

Brighton's statement answer, erecting Europe's first purpose-built women's football stadium, is one solution, but many WSL clubs do not have the space, money or resources to do likewise.

Brighton plan Europe's first purpose-built £80m women's stadium

Bespoke women's football stadiums? Why US sides are making the move

From next season, Chelsea will play all home WSL fixtures at Stamford Bridge, joining Arsenal, Aston Villa and Everton in committing to home venues with improved transport links and better facilities.

Tottenham, Manchester United and Brighton will host marquee fixtures at their main stadiums, though the majority of matches will be at their smaller grounds.

When it comes to engaging fans when bums are on seats, in stadiums or at home, there is a need to refine communication and marketing strategies.

BBC Sport's 2025 Summer of Sport research revealed social media is the principal way to reach younger audiences, with 35% of 18-24-year-olds using social networks as their primary method of keeping up to date with women's football.

Social media also ranks highly among 25-34-year-old fans, second only to watching live.

"I'll go to social media before Google or somewhere else. Everyone is already talking about it," affirms Major.

WSL fixtures are released on Thursday, 30 July and with the expanded 14-team format, there is potential to draw more eyes than ever in the 2026-27 season.

Then there is the Lionesses factor.

The success and visibility of Sarina Wiegman's side has had a huge impact on fan engagement domestically, with Chloe Kelly's penalty heroics in last summer's Euro 2025 final triumph a "watershed moment" for women's football marketing.

Next summer's World Cup in Brazil will further bolster excitement, though England must navigate two play-off rounds to guarantee their place.

For now, it is over to the clubs to see if they can rectify existing issues and harness the power of the national team to push growth to the next level.

title: Why Rogers and Palmer will thrive together in Alonso's Chelsea
description: Why Morgan Rogers' skillset means he and fellow attacking midfielder Cole Palmer will prosper in Xabi Alonso's Chelsea.
fullText:
Morgan Rogers was quick to mention one of his closest friends, Cole Palmer, when he signed for Chelsea from Aston Villa.

"We've been speaking about this for a while - that we would always love to play together," said the £117m attacking midfielder.

"He's been non-stop ringing my phone, texting me, and I can't wait. That's probably the most special thing, playing with one of your best friends and being around him every day. It's something I'm really excited about."

Both men might be keen to play together... but can new Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso find the system to accommodate two such similar profiles?

We take a closer look at Rogers' skillset and assess how Alonso might set up his side this season.

It is difficult to clearly define Rogers by a fixed position.

As with all players, getting the best from them means appreciating the wider role they are capable of. A player's ideal role can also change depending on the players around them and the opposition's set-up.

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery gave Rogers a major role in the side's recent successes, something that contributed to his hefty transfer fee.

Emery's system is built upon defensive solidity, often in a 4-4-2 shape off the ball. Villa often spent long periods without the ball before attacking into large areas of space at pace.

This is a style of play that suits Rogers, who combines impressive ball-striking with standout athleticism.

Last season, he generally played on the left of a 4-2-3-1, narrowing in from the wing and leaving the left-back to provide the width.

From here he often opted to curl the ball into the far post with his stronger right foot, but could just as easily drag his shot inside the near post at the last moment.

Out of possession, Rogers usually defended as a left midfielder in Emery's 4-4-2 but is capable of pressing in the front two alongside a traditional number nine.

His positional versatility allows him to play as a narrow winger on both the left and right side of attack, before making runs akin to a centre-forward.

He consistently injects pace into his team's attack with his direct nature both with and without the ball.

Alonso's system has overarching principles, with the Spaniard seeking to dominate the ball and set up attacks in the opponent's half for long periods.

This is different to the approach that got the best out of Rogers for Villa.

Although this might raise some alarm bells, last season there was a rise in man-to-man pressure high up the pitch - making playing out from the back tougher.

The best teams in the league, in response, have prioritised players who are capable of holding the ball up, carrying the ball over big distances, and able to beat their marker one against one.

With opposition sides matching up man-for-man, the game then becomes a series of one-against-one duels, so strong players who can beat their defender are exceptionally valuable.

All of these descriptions line up with Rogers' strengths.

Against intense pressure, teams have opted to play longer passes into their forwards, skipping build-up altogether. Rogers is more than capable of receiving such direct passes.

Although a possession-based coach, Alonso has shown the flexibility and intelligence to look for solutions against man-to-man pressure.

The Chelsea manager is associated with a short passing game, but after Leverkusen lost the 2024 Europa League final to Atalanta - who man-mark intensely across the pitch - he showed pragmatism in his analysis.

"We probably tried to play too many passes in the first phase, when we should have tried to attract the first player and then go long a bit more," he said.

Rogers gives him a solution to the problems of a tactical landscape that has an emphasis on man-to-man pressing.

Understanding Alonso's set-up can help to explain how Rogers and Palmer could thrive together.

Irrespective of whether the Spaniard sets Chelsea up in a back four or a five, his team will move in the same shape in attacking possession, namely 3-2-2-3 or 3-2-5.

Many of Rogers' best moments at Villa were in the inside-left channel. Alonso is likely to try to position him there when Chelsea have the ball.

This means width on the left would have to come from another player - either a wing-back if Chelsea defend with a back five or a winger if it is a back four. In the latter formation, Rogers would be positioned more centrally from the start.

One of the reasons Alonso will have championed the Rogers signing is his ability to play across the attack - most recently demonstrated as a right winger for England against Argentina.

Palmer similarly thrives in-field - but on the right half of the pitch. Both players in possession could be positioned alongside each other in the middle of the pitch in a 3-2-2-3 behind a striker such as Joao Pedro.

Rogers can take advantage of big spaces, but his combination play, central passing, and ball-striking from the edge of the box also mean that when he is surrounded by players on a similar wavelength - such as Palmer - it is a potent strategy for playing through structured defences.

A key part of Alonso's game model is prioritising short passes to ensure his players are well placed to counter-press if the ball is lost.

Rogers' combination play plus his physicality make him a good fit for this plan and his ability to repeatedly make runs in behind is something Palmer will seek to exploit.

In Alonso's preferred 3-2-2-3 when in possession, Rogers in the left number 10 position and Palmer in the right number 10 position is likely to work best.

To get them in these areas in attack, Alonso can start with them in those positions, ahead of a back five using wing-backs either side of them. This was his usual formation during his success at Leverkusen.

When starting from a 4-2-3-1, this can be achieved with one of the two starting as a number 10 with the other inverting centrally from the wing, with a full-back pushing up on that flank. Width on the other side would be held in this situation by a winger.

Whether leaning into the longstanding chemistry of the duo, who won the FA Youth Cup together at Manchester City in 2020, will bear fruit remains to be seen.

What is certain is that Rogers is a versatile, Premier League-proven player whose skillset has synergy with many of the aspects required in what Alonso will try to do at Chelsea.

title: The two days which could make or break Fury-AJ
description: BBC Sport looks at how a proposed bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua hinges on a 24-hour-period between Friday and Saturday.
fullText:
After more than a decade of posturing and power struggles - a soap opera of warring promoters, shifting managers, fractured television deals and failed negotiations - it has finally come down to this.

The biggest fight in British boxing history - Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua - hangs on one final two-day stretch.

On Friday, Fury, 37, fights Mariusz Wach in the unlikely surroundings of Pattaya, Thailand. There is no broadcaster, only a modest crowd expected and a 46-year-old opponent.

The following evening, almost 4,000 miles away in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, Joshua returns against Kristian Prenga - an Albanian knockout artist whom even the most hardened boxing fans would struggle to pick out of a line-up.

If all goes to plan, Fury will leave Thailand within hours of beating Wach, board a private jet and fly to Saudi Arabia, where he is expected to climb through the ropes and finally stand face-to-face with Joshua.

The contracts are signed but, especially in boxing, the ink is never truly dry until the opening bell rings.

Fury lighter than opponent for first time in 15 years

Pre-fight Joshua not ready for death of friends to sink in

'Would Beckham do it?' - Fury stands by Thailand fight

Fury and Joshua, 36, have defined British heavyweight boxing for more than a decade without ever sharing a professional ring.

Yet they arrive at this moment for very different reasons. For Joshua, it is about far more than shaking off ring rust.

The two-time world champion has not fought since surviving the car crash in Nigeria last December that claimed the lives of close friends Sina Ghami and Latif "Latz" Ayodele.

Joshua has spoken about the emotional toll of the tragedy. Promoter Eddie Hearn believes boxing has "saved" Joshua - just as it did when he first took up the sport as a troubled 19-year-old searching for direction.

"When you come off an incident like that and an accident like that, I guess people say, 'Will you ever be the same?' Certainly everything he's shown in training camp, after he went through all the near-impossible work to get himself in that position, shows that he is," Hearn told BBC Sport.

"The questions that you ask yourself, the moments where your head hits the pillow at night and it's just you in your room, what's going on inside between those two ears?"

There was also the physical recovery.

"In the early stages, just a slight movement in bed would be excruciating pain," Hearn said.

"To getting back on the bike and doing two hours' cycling when he couldn't move his upper body, and going through the physio sessions, that was an incredible journey."

Fury, who briefly retired after back-to-back defeats by Oleksandr Usyk, already had the comeback fight many felt he needed when comfortably outpointing Arslanbek Makhmudov in April.

BBC boxing pundit Steve Bunce is not convinced another outing was necessary.

"The fight against Makhmudov was perfect, it was the dream fight for a fighter after a long break," Bunce says.

"You could see he wasn't bothered about the stoppage, he just needed those priceless rounds. But this fight against Wach is one he will not lose under any circumstances. It's ceremonial."

Fury's trip to Thailand appears to be as much about publicity as preparation.

The cameras for the third season of his Netflix documentary, 'At Home with the Furys' will be rolling at ringside with exclusive access. No other broadcaster will be present.

It would rank among the biggest upsets in heavyweight history if Fury lost to a man who turns 47 this year and has lost seven of his past 10 fights.

"Fury should dominate but the biggest risk for me is that he looks awful," Bunce says.

"Also, Tyson might find out that he has lost something and senses some flaws in himself."

There is a fraction more jeopardy for Joshua. Prenga is largely an unknown quantity to the wider public, but his record demands respect: 20 wins, 20 knockouts and one defeat.

"This fight is designed to be competitive, but not too competitive," Hearn says.

"He's never boxed at AJ's level, but until you fight at that level, you actually don't know if you're good enough. But he's decent, he's game and he's dangerous."

The greater threat to the Fury-AJ super-fight is injury.

"Tyson is too smart and clever and I think Wach won't be using his elbows or head. There will be some sort of gentleman's agreement," Bunce adds.

"He could injure his arm or leg. At Tyson's age, with hard training camps, that can happen. It could also happen to Joshua."

If both men emerge unscathed, attention will quickly turn to Jeddah. The hope is that Fury will travel straight from Thailand and join Joshua in the ring for an official announcement.

"Perhaps Fury will get on a private jet and arrive in Jeddah - give it a bit of drama in the style of WWE," Bunce said.

"But if they both win, you have to announce it right then. You can't let it slip."

Remarkably, the two have only ever shared a ring once before - a semi-mythical sparring session back in 2010 when Fury was a 21-year-old prospect with an undefeated professional record and Joshua was a raw 20-year-old amateur.

Hearn is a little less certain Fury will make the journey to Saudi Arabia.

"We hope, now that the contracts are signed, we'll see him on Saturday," Hearn said.

"I would suggest most people would get on a plane, but he is Tyson Fury."

Saudi Arabia powerbroker Turki Alalshikh, a key figure in bringing together Fury v Joshua, has said that for the fight to happen on British soil, it would require a middle-of-the-night start time at Wembley Stadium to cater for prime-time American audiences on Netflix.

Such a plan would require extending Wembley's usual 11pm curfew, although sources close to London Mayor Sadiq Khan indicated the city would be willing to help make it happen.

Industry whispers point towards Las Vegas or New York, while Hearn says Joshua's contract stipulates the fight must happen in the UK - but he has not ruled out a move to America.

The prospect of the biggest British fight in history taking place thousands of miles away is a difficult one for many UK fans to accept.

Whatever unfolds across these extraordinary coming hours, we are about to find out whether the biggest fight in British boxing history is going to be a reality or destined to remain the sport's greatest what-if.

title: NFL Analyst Identifies the Vikings Player Under the Most Pressure
description: Minnesota Vikings tight end T. J. Hockenson could be in line to have a big year, and The Athletic’s Alec Lewis seems optimistic about where the tight end could head in 2026.The tight end can produce at a high level that much is clear. Just take the 2025 season for example.
fullText:
Minnesota Vikings tight end T. J. Hockenson could be in line to have a big year, and The Athletic’s Alec Lewis seems optimistic about where the tight end could head in 2026.

The tight end can produce at a high level that much is clear. Just take the 2025 season for example. He played in only 15 games, but recorded 51 receptions on 66 targets, for 438 yards and three touchdowns. It was the lowest total of his career, but he still managed to produce at a high level. He missed the final two games of the season with a shoulder injury.

Now, Lewis is predicting this season will be important with a new contract looming.

Critical season forthcoming. Hockenson’s current contract voids after 2026. He is 29 years old. Proving he can produce like he did pre-ACL tear could net another hefty deal.

The 2025 season saw him record 66 receptions for 438 yards and three touchdowns. The tight end was still trying to find that explosiveness he lost following his late-2023 ACL\MCL tear. It showed in some aspects of his play as well. He had a 5.2 average depth of target, which was one of the lower numbers of his career. In addition to not running deeper routes, he also had four drops on 66 targets. This saw him record a 6% drop rate, which was the highest of his career.

In addition, Hockenson was forced to block more. This was a result of inconsistent quarterback play and poor offensive line play. Overall, it was not a good season for a tight end who was one of the most explosive in the NFL at one time.

For his Vikings career, he has recorded 223 receptions for 2,213 yards and eight touchdowns. His best season came in 2023. He had 95 receptions for 960 yards and six touchdowns. He also had a 74.8 catch percentage. To be fair, he recorded the highest catch percentage of his Vikings career at 77.3 in 2025. However, his production was obviously down.

Now, he is looking to bounce back in a major way. The injuries, in combination with an inconsistent offense, have led him to having a reduced role in some ways. This could be his biggest chance to get a strong season under his belt. If he can stay healthy and show that he can perform with the quarterback under center, then he should be able to land himself that new deal. However, the ACL injury certainly looms large, especially for a player who takes pride in receiving and blocking. How he can move this season, two years removed from injury, is going to be important.

When healthy, Hockenson is a valuable piece of the offense. He showed that explosiveness with the Detroit Lions, and he has the opportunity to show it with the Minnesota Vikings as well. At his peak, he can be a game-changer for any offense. Now, he just has to get back to that. Of course, that is easier said than done, but the Vikings’ offense would undoubtedly benefit from him being healthy, as well as taking on more responsibility in the passing game. This will undoubtedly be a storyline heading into training camp.

title: Insider Sets High Price Tag for Potential Blockbuster Wizards Trade
description: This would be a major deal. The post Insider Sets High Price Tag for Potential Blockbuster Wizards Trade appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Washington Wizards have given strong signals that they plan to keep Anthony Davis, and he has reciprocated their intent. However, trade speculation continues to swirl around Davis, who could be the key to one team’s goal of landing LeBron James.

That sets the stage for a potentially lucrative opportunity for the Wizards.

Of course, such an opportunity, in all likelihood, would mean the Wizards would be less competitive in the East this coming season than they are setting out to be.

ESPN’s Shams Charania spoke candidly about the Golden State Warriors’ pursuit of Davis, noting that it would take a hefty haul to pry him loose from the Wizards.

The Warriors conversation, that was definitely alive right before free agency started. That’s why Draymond Green opted out. He opted out of $27.7 million. That surprised the Warriors. That surprised everyone around the league. But that was done to give the Warriors the flexibility to try to get LeBron James and Anthony Davis. Those conversations for AD have gone nowhere for the Warriors, from my understanding,” Charania said on the “Pat McAfee Show” on July 23.

“I don’t think that’s going to be a conversation, because it’s at a point now where if the Warriors were to get in that ballgame, they would have to give up multiple first-round picks, multiple draft picks, multiple swaps, all this other stuff.”

Charania noted some teams would argue Davis is worth it if that also lands James.

“If you’re the Warriors, that’s the give and take that you have there,” he said. “The domino effect, that was in play before free agency started. Now that we’re 20 days in, there’s nothing left.”

Wizards general manager Will Dawkins has set the organization up in an interesting position, with an intriguing mix of veterans like Davis and Trae Young and several recent first-round picks, including No. 1 selection in 2026 AJ Dybantsa and 2025 No. 2 pick Alex Sarr.

title: Former Los Angeles Lakers star named most overrated player in NBA
description: A former Los Angeles Lakers star has been named the NBA's most overrated player.  Davis, 33, was recently given the distinction of being the league's most overrated player by Zach Buckley of Bleacher Report, who pointed to Davis' inconsistent availability and declining production as reasons why he topped the list.
fullText:
Former Los Angeles Lakers star named most overrated player in NBA originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

A former Los Angeles Lakers star has been named the NBA's most overrated player.

That player is Washington Wizards forward Anthony Davis, who was one of the best players in the league at one point, but has been hampered by injury issues as of late.

Davis, 33, was recently given the distinction of being the league's most overrated player by Zach Buckley of Bleacher Report, who pointed to Davis' inconsistent availability and declining production as reasons why he topped the list.

"If guaranteed a clean bill of health, would Anthony Davis be the most impactful player on this list? Maybe. But that's a moot point when he can be guaranteed nothing of the sort," Buckley wrote.

". . . Things that used to be automatic with AD are, at best, major question marks. He'll have flashes of his old dominant days and they might get covered similarly since he's such a notable name, but when his employer is merely hoping to get 50 games from him at this point (a number he missed in three of the past six seasons), things have clearly changed."

Davis will have an opportunity to prove Buckley, and other doubters, wrong this upcoming season, which will be his first full season as a member of the Washington Wizards.

title: Pundit thinks Lamine Yamal is stronger Ballon d’Or candidate than Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane
description: The FC Bayern star seems to get points docked for being well-rounded and willing to help his teams.
fullText:
William Gallas has effectively ruled Harry Kane out of the Ballon d’Or race following England’s disappointing World Cup campaign.

The Bayern Munich striker remains one of the most prolific goalscorers in world football, but Gallas believes individual numbers alone will not be enough to earn Kane the game’s biggest individual prize. According to the former France international, the World Cup played a major role in changing the conversation,“ Gallas told iPredicta. “Harry Kane didn’t have a great, great World Cup. Even if he scored goals, his World Cup was not the best. So, forget about Harry Kane winning the Ballon d’Or.

“You have to be focused on players like Lamine Yamal, who I think is the number one because he won the World Cup and his performances were good, despite having an injury at the start.”

It is a brutally dismissive assessment of Kane’s chances, but Gallas is highlighting the importance of the biggest stage. Kane may have continued to deliver in front of goal, but the Ballon d’Or is rarely decided by statistics alone.

As a counterpoint, it could also be strongly argued that Yamal was only the third or fourth best player on his own team at the World Cup. For Gallas, though, Yamal has the strongest case after helping Spain win the World Cup while producing the kind of performances that capture global attention. The young Barcelona star has already established himself as one of the most influential players in the world, and his tournament only strengthened his claim.

Kane will likely remain in the conversation because of his extraordinary goal scoring record. However, if the World Cup is the deciding factor, Gallas believes the Bayern Munich striker has already fallen behind the leading contenders.

title: WNBA Spokesman Issues Statement After Sabrina Ionescu Denies Receiving WNBA 3-Point Contest Invite
description: It was hard to imagine that Sabrina Ionescu would not be on the list of contestants for this year’s WNBA All-Star 3-Point Contest. Which is exactly why so many quickly concluded she must have declined the invitation when her name was absent from the announcement.
fullText:
It was hard to imagine that Sabrina Ionescu would not be on the list of contestants for this year’s WNBA All-Star 3-Point Contest. Which is exactly why so many quickly concluded she must have declined the invitation when her name was absent from the announcement.

Ionescu herself, however, has since come out to directly challenge that assumption, stating that she cannot decline an offer she never officially received in the first place. But a WNBA spokesman has clarified the league’s process in such matters via ESPN’s Alexa Philippou.

“Sabrina Ionescu said yesterday re: her involvement in the 3-point contest, ‘I can’t decline an offer I never officially got invited to,'” Philippou posted on her X account on Thursday. “From a WNBA spokesperson: ‘Our general process is to reach out to agents to determine a player’s interest, and some accept and some decline.'”

“Seems notable that Sabrina said she never got ‘officially invited‘ while the league said it generally reaches out ‘to determine a player’s interest.’ Have to imagine there was a dialogue of some sorts between the camps.”

Philippou’s post suggests that both Sabrina Ionescu‘s and the spokesman’s statements could simultaneously be accurate. As Ionescu said, she never received a formal invitation directly. And based on the spokesman’s explanation, it appears the WNBA never issued any official invite to begin with. Instead, they likely informally contacted her agent to gauge her interest before they formally initiated any process.

To a large extent, Lynx guard Kayla McBride’s own account seems to further authenticate the spokesman’s process description. McBride, who also does not feature among the contestants, revealed she too only received what amounted to a half-hearted invitation, communicated informally through a text from her agent rather than any kind of formal outreach.

Both McBride and Ionescu have history with the three-point contest. McBride’s most notable run came during the 2019 competition, where she finished as the runner-up behind Shekinna Stricklen of the Connecticut Sun.

Ionescu’s résumé in the competition, however, is in an entirely different category. She is a two-time WNBA 3-Point Contest champion, winning both times she has participated. She also holds the all-time basketball record for the most points scored in a single round across both the WNBA and NBA competitions combined. And she famously took on Stephen Curry in the NBA’s version of the contest, losing only narrowly in one of the most memorable moments the event has ever produced.

Given all of that, it is no surprise that fans were eager to see her back in this year’s competition. And why many appear visibly disappointed when she was not included. But regardless of how or whether she was invited, Ionescu has made clear that she is genuinely excited for the contest. She, in fact, looks forward to seeing who comes out on top.

title: Beatdown roundtable: favorite almost-signing in Ravens history
description: Baltimore Beatdown’s staff offers their favorite almost-signing in Ravens franchise history.
fullText:
Baltimore Beatdown is all about Almost Ravens this week! In addition to our reader-driven bracket narrowing down the biggest near-acquisitions in team history, our staff will also be providing their opinions on their favorite moves the Ravens almost pulled off. Today, we’re focusing on trades:

The Ravens’ near-signing of future Hall of Fame linebacker Bobby Wagner in 2022 is a really interesting one. Wagner himself had a solid year in Los Angeles with another second-team All-Pro berth and may have stayed in Baltimore for a few years. And the Ravens likely would not have traded for Roquan Smith during the regular season and signed him to a long-term extension that has not aged well. Smith has been great in Baltimore, but it’s fair to wonder if a more moderate price for Wagner plus the second-round pick the Ravens sent to Chicago would have been a better allocation of resources. – Nikhil Mehta

My favorite player the Ravens almost signed is Darius Slay. While Slay was on the backend of his NFL journey in 2023-24, he was still playing well and likely would have been a great fit in Baltimore. Placing him alongside Marlon Humphrey, Kyle Hamilton and company could have paid dividends. Slay likely would helped sure up the team’s secondary and alleviate some of their issues allowing big passing plays in recent seasons. He profiled as the prototypical veteran who the Ravens sign and get high-level play out of late in their career. – Frank Platko

My personal favorite player the Ravens almost signed was Za’Darius Smith. When the deal with “Z” was announced, I was so thrilled for him to come back as a Raven. Looking back on it now, if Smith’s deal had stayed, with Mike Macdonald as the defensive coordinator in 2022 and 2023, he could have been an anchor for what would become one of the NFL’s most feared defenses while Macdonald was in Baltimore (once Macdonald got through his early kinks in 2022). Instead, everything went haywire. Smith back out of Baltimore’s four-year deal, then signed a three-year deal with Minnesota. He was then traded to Cleveland before the 2023 season, traded to Detroit in the middle of the 2024 season, signed with the Eagles at the start of the 2025 season, then retired after five games. I was devastated when I learned Smith had backed out with the Ravens.. – Zach Canter

While not my favorite player among the bunch, Ryan Grant has to be my personal favorite “almost signing” of the Ravens, purely for the hilarity that ensued. It’s no secret that Baltimore has historically struggled to field quality wide receivers, and this was never more true than the final few years of Joe Flacco’s tenure with the team. Entering the 2018 offseason, the Ravens desperately needed wide receiver help after the Jeremy Maclin signing did not pan out the season prior. Baltimore chose to bring in two veteran free agents ahead of the draft in John Brown and Ryan Grant. Brown, a speedster coming from Arizona, was given a modest one-year deal worth up to $6.5 million with incentives. Grant, on the other hand, was oddly given a four-year, $29 million deal despite totaling just 985 receiving yards in his first four seasons with Washington. Fans were rightfully puzzled by the signing. As with Maxx Crosby though, a failed physical nixed the deal, which ultimately led to the team signing a much more accomplished veteran wide receiver in Michael Crabtree, who had just been released by the Raiders. Grant fizzled out, playing just two more seasons in the NFL, ultimately proving the Ravens right for backing out of the deal due to health concerns, but the decision to give him such a contract in the first place baffles me to this day. – Dustin Cox

Who is the biggest Almost-Raven in franchise history? | Baltimore Beatdown

title: Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon presenting Adam Vinatieri for Hall of Fame induction
description: Adam Vinatieri asked Colts' owner Carlie Irsay Gordon to present at his Hall of Fame induction ceremony.
fullText:
Former Indianapolis Colts' kicker Adam Vinatieri will be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame on Aug. 8, and principal owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon will be the presenter.

The Colts' social media team captured the moment when Vinatieri asked Irsay-Gordon to present.

"I just wanted to come in and say thank you so much for everything that you and your family have done for me. It's been such a wonderful ride," Vinatieri said. "I can't even express to you how much you guys have all meant to me and I'd be super, super honored if you'd present me."

Vinatieri added, "If you're willing to do it, I would absolutely love it if you would put me into the Hall of Fame."

Mike Chappell of FOX59 posted that had Vinatieri been a first-ballot Hall of Famer, late owner Jim Irsay would have been the presenter.

a special moment for @cirsay from future HOFer @adamvinatieri. pic.twitter.com/GXcpkOaG16

— Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) July 23, 2026

Vinatieri will enter the Hall of Fame as the NFL's all-time leader in career points. He also holds the record for most consecutive field goals made with 44, career field goals made with 599, and most postseason points as well.

Vinatieri spent14 seasons with the Colts, where he made 85.3 percent of his field goal attempts. In the playoffs, Vinatieri made 81.2% of those attempts.

He was a three-time Pro Bowler and a three-time All-Pro in his career. Vinatieri also won four Super Bowls, including one with the Colts in 2006.

Vinatieri will also be inducted into the Colts' Ring of Honor in Week 6 of this upcoming season.

title: Shaquille O'Neal: LeBron James Ending Career With Cavaliers Would Be 'Historical'
description: Shaquille O'Neal thinks it would be cool to see LeBron James finish his NBA career with the Cleveland Cavaliers.
fullText:
NBA legend Shaquille O'Neal believes LeBron James ending his career with the Cleveland Cavaliers would be "historical."

LeBron began his NBA career with the Cavaliers back in 2003. He played for the franchise from 2003-10 before going to the Miami Heat from 2010-14. The Akron native then returned to Cleveland from 2014-18 and helped delivered the team's first title in franchise history in 2016.

A future Hall of Famer, LeBron is currently a free agent for the first time since 2018. He's expected to sign with the Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Philadelphia 76ers or Minnesota Timberwolves.

Many people believe LeBron will sign with the Cavaliers. Cleveland assistant general manager Brandon Weems was with LeBron in Ohio a few weekends ago.

Weems is one of LeBron's closest friends.

"Let me talk to you about Brandon Weems," LeBron's agent, Rich Paul of Klutch Sports Group, said on his podcast. "Brandon Weems is basically LeBron's brother. Now, he worked his own way [up], nobody gave him anything. He's earned to be in the front office of the Cavs. But that is a big feather in the cap [for Cleveland], because of Brandon Weems."

It would certainly be cool to see LeBron end his career in Cleveland. A starting lineup of James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, LeBron, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen could compete for the championship next season.

The Cavaliers made the conference finals last season, losing to the New York Knicks in four quick games. Adding LeBron could make Cleveland title favorites next season.

If Harden signs for $30 million and if Cleveland can deal Max Strus and take back no salary in return, the Cavaliers would be able to give LeBron the mid-level exception.

For the Los Angeles Lakers last season, LeBron averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists per game. He's still an elite offensive player despite being the oldest active player in the NBA.

It will be interesting to see where LeBron is playing next season. Paul recently said on his podcast that LeBron will not be "rushed" into making a decision.

"We're not going to be rushed," Paul said on the latest podcast episode of "Game Over" with Max Kellerman and Rich Paul, released Monday evening. "We're not going to be rushed. It's his choice to make and when he makes the choice, he'll make it. ... I saw Adam in New York and we discussed it. And like I said, it's still his choice. So if he doesn't really know, you can't rush it. You can't rush it."
